title.zh: 卷32 高湖 崔逞 封懿
title.en: Volume 32: Gao Hu, Cui Cheng, Feng Yi
title.raw: 卷32 高湖 崔逞 封懿 Volume 32: Gao Hu, Cui Cheng, Feng Yi

sentences.zh: 高湖 崔逞 封懿

translations.literal: Gao Hu, Cui Cheng, Feng Yi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hu, Cui Cheng, and Feng Yi

sentences.zh: 高湖，字大淵，勃海蓨人也。

translations.literal: Gao Hu, styled Dayuan, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hu, whose style name was Dayuan, came from Tiao in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢太傅裒之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Gao Bao, Grand Tutor of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He traced his descent to Gao Bao, Grand Tutor under the Han.

sentences.zh: [1]祖慶，慕容垂司空。

translations.literal: [1] His grandfather Qing was Minister of Works under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: [1] His grandfather Qing had served Murong Chui as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父泰，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Tai was Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tai held the post of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 湖少機敏，有器度，與兄韜俱知名於時，雅為鄉人崔逞所敬異。

translations.literal: Hu in youth was quick-witted and had breadth of character; he and his elder brother Tao were both renowned in their time, and were deeply respected and regarded as extraordinary by their fellow townsman Cui Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hu was quick and perceptive, with real breadth of character. He and his elder brother Tao were both celebrated in their day, and their fellow townsman Cui Cheng held them in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 少歷顯職，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through prominent offices and served as Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he rose through prominent posts and became Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 登國十年，垂遣其太子寶來伐也，湖言於垂曰：「魏，燕之與國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dengguo, when Chui sent his heir apparent Bao to attack, Hu spoke to Chui, saying: "Wei is Yan's allied state.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dengguo, when Murong Chui sent his heir apparent Bao on campaign against Wei, Hu remonstrated with Chui: "Wei is Yan's ally.

sentences.zh: 彼有內難，此遣赴之；

translations.literal: When they had internal troubles, we sent men to their aid;
translations.idiomatic: When they faced internal troubles, we sent forces to help them;

sentences.zh: 此有所求，彼無違者。

translations.literal: when we had requests, they did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: when we made requests, they did not refuse us.

sentences.zh: 和好多年，行人相繼。

translations.literal: For many years there was friendship, and envoys followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Friendship had lasted many years, with envoys traveling back and forth without cease.

sentences.zh: 往求馬不得，遂留其弟，曲在於此，非彼之失。

translations.literal: Formerly we sought horses and did not obtain them, so we detained his younger brother—the fault lies on this side, not theirs.
translations.idiomatic: When we once asked for horses and were refused, we detained his younger brother; the wrong was on our side, not theirs.

sentences.zh: 政當敦修舊好，乂寧國家，而復令太子率眾遠伐。

translations.literal: We ought rather to earnestly restore the old friendship and bring peace to the states, yet again the heir is sent to lead troops on a distant campaign.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to renew the old friendship in earnest and settle the realm in peace, yet now the heir is sent to lead an army on a distant campaign.

sentences.zh: 且魏主雄略，兵馬精強，險阻艱難，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wei ruler is bold in strategy, his troops and horses elite and strong, and the passes difficult—we have tasted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Wei ruler is a bold strategist, his soldiers and horses first-rate, and the terrain treacherous—we have learned that at our cost.

sentences.zh: 太子富於春秋，意果心銳，輕敵好勝，難可獨行。

translations.literal: The heir is still young in years, his intent keen and heart sharp, he underestimates the enemy and loves victory, and is hard put to go alone.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is still young, bold and eager, prone to despise the enemy and hunger for victory—he should not be sent alone.

sentences.zh: 兵凶戰危，願以深慮。

translations.literal: Arms are inauspicious and battle perilous—I beg deep consideration.
translations.idiomatic: War is inauspicious and battle perilous; I beg Your Majesty to weigh this deeply.

sentences.zh: 」言頗切厲。

translations.literal: " His words were quite stern and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: " His words were stern and urgent.

sentences.zh: 垂怒，免湖官。

translations.literal: Chui was angry and dismissed Hu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chui flew into a rage and stripped Hu of his post.

sentences.zh: 既而寶果敗於參合。

translations.literal: Before long Bao was indeed defeated at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bao was indeed defeated at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 寶立，乃起湖為征虜將軍、燕郡太守。

translations.literal: When Bao took the throne, Hu was raised to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Administrator of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao succeeded to the throne, Hu was reappointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Administrator of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 寶走和龍，兄弟交爭，湖見其衰亂，遂率戶三千歸國。

translations.literal: Bao fled to Helong; the brothers contended with one another; Hu saw the decline and disorder and thereupon led three thousand households to submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao fled to Helong and his brothers fell to fighting among themselves, Hu saw the realm crumbling and led three thousand households to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜爵東阿侯，加右將軍，總代東諸部。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor enfeoffed him as Marquis of Dong'a, added the title General of the Right, and put him in overall charge of the eastern tribes of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu enfeoffed him as Marquis of Dong'a, promoted him to General of the Right, and placed him in overall command of the eastern tribal divisions of Dai.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，除寧西將軍、涼州鎮都大將，鎮姑臧，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizu he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Commander of the Garrison of Liang province, garrisoning Guzang, and his benevolent governance was notable.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Commander of the Liangzhou garrison, stationed at Guzang, where his benevolent rule won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 年七十，卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮西將軍、秦州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General Who Guards the West and Governor of Qin province, with the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as General Who Guards the West and Governor of Qin province, with the temple name Jing ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 有四子。

translations.literal: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 第三子謐，字安平，有文武才度。

translations.literal: The third son Mi, styled Anping, had talent in both civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Mi, styled Anping, possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 天安中，[2]以功臣子召入禁中，除中散，專典秘閣。

translations.literal: In the Tian'an era, [2] as the son of a meritorious minister he was summoned into the inner palace, appointed Central Scribe, and put in sole charge of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tian'an era, [2] as the son of a meritorious official he was summoned into the inner palace, appointed Central Scribe, and placed in sole charge of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 肅勤不倦，高宗深重之，拜祕書郎。

translations.literal: Solemn and diligent without tiring, Emperor Gaozong held him in deep regard and appointed him Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn, diligent, and tireless, he won Emperor Gaozong's deep regard and was appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 謐以墳典殘缺，奏請廣訪羣書，大加繕寫。

translations.literal: Mi, because the canonical texts were damaged and incomplete, memorialized requesting a broad search for books and a great program of copying and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the classics damaged and incomplete, Mi memorialized for a broad search of books and a major program of copying and repair.

sentences.zh: 由是代京圖籍，莫不審正。

translations.literal: From this the books and records of the capital of Dai were without exception put in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the books and records held at the Dai capital were all brought into proper order.

sentences.zh: 顯祖之御寧光宮也，謐恒侍講讀，拜蘭臺御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu resided at Ningguang Palace, Mi constantly attended him for lectures and reading, and was appointed Censor of the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xianzu resided at Ningguang Palace, Mi regularly attended him for lectures and was appointed Censor of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 尋轉治書，掌攝內外，彈糾非法，當官而行，無所畏避，甚見稱賞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Drafting Documents, overseeing both inner and outer affairs, impeaching illegal conduct, acting according to office without fear or evasion, and was greatly praised.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Drafting Documents, overseeing affairs within and without the palace, impeaching wrongdoing, discharging his duties without fear or favor, and won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 延興二年九月卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yanxing he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the second year of Yanxing, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，追贈使持節、侍中、都督青徐齊濟兗五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、太尉公，青州刺史，[3]諡武貞公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, Qi, Ji, and Yan provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Taiwei, and Governor of Qing province, [3] with the posthumous title Duke Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over Qing, Xu, Qi, Ji, and Yan provinces, the title General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Taiwei, and the governorship of Qing, [3] with the posthumous title Duke Wuzhen ("Martial and Upright").

sentences.zh: 妻叔孫氏，陳留郡君。

translations.literal: His wife was Lady Shusun, Lady of Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, of the Shusun clan, held the title Lady of Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 長子樹生。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shusheng.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Shusheng.

sentences.zh: 性通達，重節義，交結英雄，不事生產，有識者並宗奇之。

translations.literal: By nature open and penetrating, he valued integrity and righteousness, befriended heroes, did not engage in production, and men of insight all regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Open and broad-minded by nature, he prized integrity and righteousness, sought out men of heroic stature, and cared nothing for livelihood; thoughtful observers all regarded him as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕侵掠，高祖詔懷朔鎮將陽平王頤率眾討之，頤假樹生鎮遠將軍、都將，先驅有功。

translations.literal: When the Rouran raided and plundered, Emperor Gaozu ordered the garrison commander of Huaishuo, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, to lead troops against them; Yi lent Shusheng the titles General Who Pacifies the Distance and Chief Commander, and as vanguard he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontiers, Emperor Gaozu ordered Yi, Prince of Yangping and commander of Huaishuo, to lead a punitive force; Yi lent Shusheng the ranks of General Who Pacifies the Distance and chief commander, and Shusheng distinguished himself in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 樹生尚氣俠，意在浮沉自適，不願職位，辭不受賞，論者高之。

translations.literal: Shusheng prized chivalric spirit, his intent being to rise and fall as suited him and not to seek office; he declined rewards, and commentators held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng was a man of chivalrous spirit who wished only to go where fortune carried him, not to chase office; he declined rewards, and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 居宅數有赤光紫氣之異，鄰伍驚恐，僉謂怪變，宅不可居。

translations.literal: At his residence there were repeatedly strange signs of red light and purple vapors; neighbors were alarmed and all said it was an uncanny transformation and the house could not be lived in.
translations.idiomatic: Strange red lights and purple vapors repeatedly appeared over his house; neighbors were terrified and agreed it was an omen—the dwelling was unfit to live in.

sentences.zh: 樹生曰：「何往非善。

translations.literal: Shusheng said: "Where one goes, is it not all for the good?
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng said, "Wherever one goes can be for the good.

sentences.zh: 」[4]安之自若。

translations.literal: " [4] He settled himself at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " [4] He remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 雅好音律，常以絲竹自娛。

translations.literal: He was fond of music and often amused himself with strings and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and often entertained himself with string and wind instruments.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，北州大亂，詔發眾軍，廣開募賞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang the northern provinces were in great disorder; an edict mobilized the armies and broadly opened recruitment with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era the northern provinces fell into chaos; an edict mobilized the armies and opened recruitment with generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 以樹生有威略，授以大都督，令率勁勇，鎮捍舊蕃。

translations.literal: Because Shusheng had authority and strategy, he was given the title Great Commander and ordered to lead crack troops to garrison and defend the old frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shusheng had both authority and strategic talent, he was appointed Great Commander and ordered to lead elite troops to hold the old frontier.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the era, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，追贈使持節、都督冀相滄瀛殷定六州諸軍事、大將軍、太師、錄尚書事、冀州刺史，追封勃海王，諡曰文穆，妻韓氏，為勃海王國太妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Xiang, Cang, Ying, Yin, and Ding provinces, Great General, Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai, posthumous name Wenmu; his wife Lady Han became Grand Princess of the Bohai princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, supreme command over Ji, Xiang, Cang, Ying, Yin, and Ding, the ranks of Great General, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and the governorship of Ji; enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Bohai with the temple name Wenmu (" Cultured and Solemn"); his wife, Lady Han of the Han clan, became Grand Princess of the Bohai princedom.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，後贈假黃鉞、侍中、都督中外諸軍事，加後部羽葆鼓吹，餘如故，長子即齊獻武王也。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was later posthumously given the Ceremonial Axe, Palace Attendant, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, with rear guard of feathered canopy and drum escort added, the rest as before; his eldest son was the Prince Xianwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he received a further posthumous promotion: the Ceremonial Axe, Palace Attendant, and supreme command over all armies at court and in the field, with the full rear guard of canopy and drum escort, other honors unchanged. His eldest son was Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王弟琛，字永寶。

translations.literal: The prince's younger brother Chen, styled Yongbao.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's younger brother Chen, whose style name was Yongbao.

sentences.zh: 天平中，驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、御史中尉、南趙郡開國公。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era: General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Halberd with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, and Duke of the founding fief of Nan Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he held the ranks of General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Halberd with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, and founding Duke of Nan Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 子叡，襲。

translations.literal: His son Rui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子庶子。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 樹生弟翻，字飛雀，亦以器度知名。

translations.literal: Shusheng's younger brother Fan, styled Feique, was also renowned for breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng's younger brother Fan, styled Feique, was likewise known for his breadth of character.

sentences.zh: 卒於侍御中散。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Central Scribe of the Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Central Scribe of the Imperial Attendants.

sentences.zh: 元象中，贈假黃鉞、使持節、侍中、都督冀定洛瀛并肆燕恒雲朔十州諸軍事、大將軍、太傅、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史，諡曰孝宣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was posthumously given the Ceremonial Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in ten provinces including Ji, Ding, Luo, Ying, Bing, Si, Yan, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, Great General, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Taiwei, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji, with posthumous name Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was posthumously honored with the Ceremonial Axe, the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over Ji, Ding, Luo, Ying, Bing, Si, Yan, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, the ranks of Great General, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Taiwei, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and the governorship of Ji, with the temple name Xiaoxuan ("Filial and Proclaiming").

sentences.zh: 子嶽，武定末，侍中、太傅公、[5]清河郡開國公。

translations.literal: His son Yue, at the end of Wuding: Palace Attendant, Duke of Grand Preceptor, [5] founding Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, at the end of Wuding, held the posts of Palace Attendant, Duke of Grand Preceptor, [5] and founding Duke of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 謐長兄真，有志行。

translations.literal: Mi's elder brother Zhen had will and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's elder brother Zhen was a man of resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱至孝，父亡，治喪墓次，甘露白雉降集焉，有司以聞，詔標閭里。

translations.literal: The brothers were both supremely filial; when their father died, while managing the funeral at the tomb they dwelt, sweet dew and white pheasants descended and gathered there; the authorities reported it, and an edict marked their lane.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were both models of filial piety. When their father died, as they kept mourning at his tomb, sweet dew fell and white pheasants gathered there; officials reported the portents, and an edict marked their neighborhood for honor.

sentences.zh: 自涇州別駕，稍遷安定太守，甚著聲績。

translations.literal: From Vice Administrator of Jing province he was gradually promoted to Administrator of Anding, with very notable reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Vice Administrator of Jing province, he rose step by step to Administrator of Anding, where his reputation and achievements were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given General of the Dragon Cavalry and Governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General of the Dragon Cavalry and Governor of Jing province.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 帶金城太守。

translations.literal: Concurrently Administrator of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as Administrator of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 神龜初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Shengui era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Shengui era.

sentences.zh: [6]太昌元年，贈使持節、侍中、都督定相殷三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、定州刺史，諡曰武康。

translations.literal: [6] In the first year of Taichang he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ding, Xiang, and Yin provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ding province, with posthumous name Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: [6] In the first year of Taichang he was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over Ding, Xiang, and Yin, the title General of Agile Cavalry with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and the governorship of Ding, with the temple name Wukang ("Martial and Assured").

sentences.zh: 子仁，正光中，卒於河州別駕。

translations.literal: His son Ren, in the Zhenguang era, died while Vice Administrator of He province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren died in the Zhenguang era while serving as Vice Administrator of He province.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈使持節、侍中、都督青齊濟三州諸軍事、儀同三司、青州刺史，諡曰明穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Qi, and Ji provinces, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Qing province, with posthumous name Mingmu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over Qing, Qi, and Ji, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and the governorship of Qing, with the temple name Mingmu ("Bright and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 子貫，字小胡。

translations.literal: His son Guan, styled Xiaohu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan, whose style name was Xiaohu.

sentences.zh: 永興末，[7]通直散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫、尚食典御。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxing, [7] he was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry with Direct Access, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongxing era, [7] he held the posts of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry with Direct Access, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 拔弟䐗兒，[8]美容貌，膂力過人，尤善弓馬。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Er, [8] handsome in appearance, strength of back surpassing others, especially skilled in bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger brother Er, [8] was handsome, possessed extraordinary physical strength, and was especially skilled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，羽林幢將。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzu he was a commander of the Feathered Forest guard company.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he served as a commander in the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，主仗令。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era he was Chief of the Ceremonial Staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangxing era he was Chief of the Ceremonial Staff.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，給事中，累遷散騎常侍、內侍長。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and through successive promotions became Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, then rose through successive promotions to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Chief Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 坐事死。

translations.literal: He died by punishment for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 子昋，字明珍，有器尚。

translations.literal: His son Ji, styled Mingzhen, had capacity and elevation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, styled Mingzhen, was a man of talent and high principle.

sentences.zh: 初除侍御史，拜奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Attending Censor, then invested as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed Attending Censor, then invested as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 與叔徽俱使西域，還至河州，遇賊攻圍，城陷見害。

translations.literal: Together with his uncle Hui he was envoy to the Western Regions; returning to He province, they met bandits besieging the city, the city fell, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He and his uncle Hui were sent together as envoys to the Western Regions. On their return at He province they were caught in a rebel siege; the city fell and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈使持節、都督冀滄二州諸軍事、征東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji and Cang provinces, General Who Conquers the East, and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, command over Ji and Cang, the title General Who Conquers the East, and the governorship of Ji.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，重贈侍中、都督青徐光三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史，諡曰文景。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was again posthumously given Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Guang provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Qing province, with posthumous name Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he received a further posthumous promotion to Palace Attendant, supreme command over Qing, Xu, and Guang, General of Agile Cavalry with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Qing, with the temple name Wenjing ("Cultured and Illustrious").

sentences.zh: 子永樂，興和中，驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、濟州刺史、陽川縣開國公。

translations.literal: His son Yongle, in the Xinghe era: General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Ji province, and founding Duke of Yangchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongle, in the Xinghe era, held the ranks of General of Agile Cavalry, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Ji, and founding Duke of Yangchuan county.

sentences.zh: 永樂弟弼，武定中，安西將軍、營州刺史、安陵縣開國男。

translations.literal: Yongle's younger brother Bi, in the Wuding era: General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Ying province, and founding Baron of Anling county.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle's younger brother Bi, in the Wuding era, was General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Ying province, and founding Baron of Anling county.

sentences.zh: 䐗兒弟徽，字榮顯，小字苟兒。

translations.literal: Er's younger brother Hui, styled Rongxian, pet name Gou'er.
translations.idiomatic: Er's younger brother Hui, styled Rongxian, was known familiarly as Gou'er.

sentences.zh: 聰敏有氣幹，為任城王澄所知賞。

translations.literal: Clever and keen, with force of spirit, he was known and appreciated by the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and forceful, he won the notice and esteem of Cheng, Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 景明中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he first took office as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he entered service as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，假員外散騎常侍，使於嚈噠，西域諸國莫不敬憚之，破洛侯、烏孫並因之以獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was provisionally Extraordinary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to the Hephthalites; the states of the Western Regions all respected and feared him, and Poluohou and Wusun both through him presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanchang era he served provisionally as Extraordinary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was sent as envoy to the Hephthalites; every state of the Western Regions respected and feared him, and Poluohou and Wusun both sent famous horses through him as tribute.

sentences.zh: 還，拜冗從僕射。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Supernumerary Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Supernumerary Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，遷射聲校尉、左中郎將、游擊將軍。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was transferred to Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, Left Commandant of the Center, and General of Mobile Striking Forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era he was promoted to Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, Left Commandant of the Center, and General of Mobile Striking Forces.

sentences.zh: 又假平西將軍、員外散騎常侍，使嚈噠。

translations.literal: Again he was provisionally General Who Pacifies the West and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and sent to the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the provisional ranks of General Who Pacifies the West and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and sent on mission to the Hephthalites.

sentences.zh: 還至枹罕，屬莫折念生反於秦隴。

translations.literal: Returning to Fuhan, it happened that Moqi Niansheng rebelled in Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reached Fuhan just as Moqi Niansheng rose in rebellion across Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 時河州刺史元祚為前刺史梁釗息景進等招引念生攻河州，祚以憂死。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of He province Yuan Zuo was induced by the former governor Liang Zhao's son Jingjin and others to draw Niansheng to attack He province; Zuo died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of He province, Yuan Zuo, had been drawn by Jingjin, son of the former governor Liang Zhao, and others into inviting Niansheng to attack He province; Zuo died of distress.

sentences.zh: 長史元永平、治中孟賓、臺使元湛，共推徽行河州事，綏接有方，兵士用命。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Yuan Yongping, Administrator of Records Meng Bin, and capital envoy Yuan Zhan together pushed Hui to act in He province affairs; his pacification and reception were well ordered, and soldiers obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Yuan Yongping, Administrator of Records Meng Bin, and capital envoy Yuan Zhan jointly urged Hui to take charge of He province; he governed with skill, and the troops obeyed him willingly.

sentences.zh: 別駕乞伏世則潛通景進，徽殺之。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Qifu Shize secretly communicated with Jingjin; Hui killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Qifu Shize was secretly in contact with Jingjin; Hui had him executed.

sentences.zh: 徵兵於吐谷渾，吐谷渾率眾救之。

translations.literal: He raised troops from the Tuyuhun; the Tuyuhun led their masses to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He called on the Tuyuhun for troops, and they marched to his relief.

sentences.zh: 景進敗，退走，奔秦州。

translations.literal: Jingjin was defeated, retreated and fled, and ran to Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjin was defeated, fled, and withdrew to Qin province.

sentences.zh: 景進尋率羌夷復來攻逼，徽遣統軍六景相馳表請師，詔徽仍行河州事。

translations.literal: Before long Jingjin led Qiang and Yi peoples again to attack and press; Hui sent the commander Liu Jingxiang with a rapid memorial requesting reinforcements, and an edict ordered Hui to continue acting in He province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingjin led Qiang and tribal forces back to press the siege. Hui sent the commander Liu Jingxiang with an urgent memorial requesting relief, and an edict confirmed him in charge of He province.

sentences.zh: 久無援救，力屈城陷，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Long without rescue, strength exhausted, the city fell, and he was killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Relief never came; his strength gave out, the city fell, and he was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，喪還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era his coffin returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era his remains were brought back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、都督冀定相瀛滄五州諸軍事、司徒公、冀州刺史，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Xiang, Ying, and Cang provinces, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Ji province, with posthumous name Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over Ji, Ding, Xiang, Ying, and Cang, the title Duke of the Ministry of Education and Governor of Ji, with the temple name Wenxuan ("Cultured and Proclaiming").

sentences.zh: 子歸義，有志烈。

translations.literal: His son Guiyi had will and fierce integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guiyi was a man of fierce resolve.

sentences.zh: 初除奉朝請，加威烈將軍。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and additionally made General of Majestic Ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and was additionally given the rank of General of Majestic Ferocity.

sentences.zh: 與父徽俱使西域。

translations.literal: Together with his father Hui he was envoy to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to the Western Regions as envoy together with his father Hui.

sentences.zh: 還都，稍遷龍驤將軍、中散大夫、西征都督，每有戰功。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was gradually promoted to General of the Dragon Cavalry, Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and Commander of the Western Campaign, and each time had military merit.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he rose step by step to General of the Dragon Cavalry, Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and Commander of the Western Campaign, distinguishing himself in battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 後沒於陣。

translations.literal: Later he perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史，諡曰孝貞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Yong province, with posthumous name Xiaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Yong, with the temple name Xiaozhen ("Filial and Upright").

sentences.zh: 子普，武定末，安南將軍、太子左衞率。

translations.literal: His son Pu, at the end of Wuding: General Who Pacifies the South and Left Commander of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu, at the end of the Wuding era, held the posts of General Who Pacifies the South and Left Commander of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 歸義弟歸彥，武定末，驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、徐州刺史、安喜縣開國男。

translations.literal: Guiyi's younger brother Guiyan, at the end of Wuding: General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Halberd with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Xu province, and founding Baron of Anxi county.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi's younger brother Guiyan, at the end of Wuding, was General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Halberd with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Xu province, and founding Baron of Anxi county.

sentences.zh: 真弟各拔，廣昌鎮將。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Geba was commander of Guangchang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Geba served as commander of the Guangchang garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 子猛虎，鄯善鎮錄事。

translations.literal: His son Menghu was recorder at the Shanshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Menghu served as recorder at the Shanshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，以至性稱，遂絕宦情。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in mourning he was famed for supreme filial nature and thereupon cut off desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father he won renown for exceptional filial devotion and thereafter renounced all ambition for office.

sentences.zh: 子元國，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Yuanguo died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanguo died young.

sentences.zh: 次顯國，武定末，撫軍將軍、汶陽男。

translations.literal: The next, Xianguo, at the end of Wuding: General Who Pacifies the Army and Baron of Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next son, Xianguo, at the end of Wuding held the ranks of General Who Pacifies the Army and Baron of Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 顯國弟達，武定中，驃騎將軍、行滄州事。

translations.literal: Xianguo's younger brother Da, in the Wuding era: General of Agile Cavalry and Acting Administrator of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: Xianguo's younger brother Da, in the Wuding era, was General of Agile Cavalry and acted as administrator of Cang province.

translations.literal: Editorial annotation marker [9].
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly note [9].

sentences.zh: 達弟永國，征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Da's younger brother Yongguo: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Da's younger brother Yongguo held the ranks of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 永國弟子國，武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Yongguo's younger brother Ziguo: General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguo's younger brother Ziguo was General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 各拔少子盛，天平中，侍中、太尉公、廣平郡開國公。

translations.literal: Geba's youngest son Sheng, in the Tianping era: Palace Attendant, Duke of Taiwei, and founding Duke of Guangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Geba's youngest son Sheng, in the Tianping era, was Palace Attendant, Duke of Taiwei, and founding Duke of Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 子子瑗，武定末，兼武衞將軍。

translations.literal: His son Ziyuan, at the end of Wuding: concurrent General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyuan, at the end of Wuding, served concurrently as General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 謐弟稚，字幼寧。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Zhi, styled Youning.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Zhi, whose style name was Youning.

sentences.zh: 薄骨律鎮將，營州刺史。

translations.literal: Commander of Bogulü garrison and Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander of the Bogulü garrison and Governor of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 子陀，字難陀。

translations.literal: His son Tuo, styled Nantuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuo, whose style name was Nantuo.

sentences.zh: 沃野鎮長。

translations.literal: Chief of Woye garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was chief of the Woye garrison.

sentences.zh: [10]卒，贈琅邪太守。

translations.literal: [10] He died and was posthumously given Administrator of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: [10] He died and was posthumously honored as Administrator of Langye.

sentences.zh: 子雍，字景雲，司徒從事。

translations.literal: His son Yong, styled Jingyun, was an attendant of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong, styled Jingyun, served as an attendant in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 後與少子思義俱奔蕭衍，卒於江南。

translations.literal: Later he and his youngest son Siyi both fled to Xiao Yan and died in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and his youngest son Siyi both defected to Xiao Yan and died in the south.

sentences.zh: 元象初，喪還，特贈使持節、散騎常侍、都督冀定瀛滄幽五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang his coffin returned; he was specially posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanxiang era his remains were brought home and he received a special posthumous promotion: the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, supreme command over Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 子思宗，武定末，中軍將軍、儀同三司、兗州刺史、上洛郡開國男。

translations.literal: His son Sizong, at the end of Wuding: General of the Central Army, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Yan province, and founding Baron of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sizong, at the end of Wuding, was General of the Central Army, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, Governor of Yan province, and founding Baron of Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 思義，特贈使持節、散騎常侍、都督青兗齊三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書僕射、儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Siyi was specially posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Yan, and Qi provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi received a special posthumous promotion: the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, supreme command over Qing, Yan, and Qi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 陀弟興，早卒。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Xing died young.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's younger brother Xing died young.

sentences.zh: 興子貴孫，晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Xing's son Guisun was Governor of Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's son Guisun served as Governor of Jin province.

sentences.zh: 湖弟恒，字叔宗，慕容垂鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: Hu's younger brother Heng, styled Shuzong, was Administrator of Julu under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's younger brother Heng, styled Shuzong, had served Murong Chui as Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，率郡降，賜爵涇縣侯，加龍驤將軍，仍守鉅鹿。

translations.literal: In the Taizu Emperor's time he led the commandery in surrender; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jing county, given the additional title General of the Dragon Cavalry, and continued to guard Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu he led his commandery in surrender, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jing county, promoted to General of the Dragon Cavalry, and continued to hold Julu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安東將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of You province, with posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of You, with the temple name Hui ("Benevolent").

sentences.zh: 子道，字始愔，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Dao, styled Shiyin, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dao, styled Shiyin, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 拜都牧令，遷鎮南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief of the Metropolitan Pasturage, then transferred to General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief of the metropolitan pasturage, then promoted to General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 未及之職，卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the new appointment.

sentences.zh: 仍以為贈，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He was still given the post posthumously, with posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was nevertheless granted posthumously, with the temple name Zhuang ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 子幹，字干奴。

translations.literal: His son Gan, styled Gannu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gan, whose style name was Gannu.

sentences.zh: 好學，寬厚有雅度。

translations.literal: He loved learning, was generous and had elegant breadth.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was generous, with a cultivated breadth of manner.

sentences.zh: 襲爵涇縣侯，後例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Jing county; later by precedent it was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Jing county, which was later reduced by precedent to a barony.

sentences.zh: 歷南青州征虜府司馬、威遠將軍、鄯善鎮遠府長史。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Major of the Pacification-Barbarians Bureau of Southern Qing province, General of Majestic Distance, and Chief Clerk of the Far-Pacification Bureau of Shanshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as major in the Pacification-Barbarians bureau of Southern Qing province, as General of Majestic Distance, and as chief clerk of the far-pacification bureau at the Shanshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 仍轉汾州後軍府長史、白水太守。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rear Army Bureau of Fen province and Administrator of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to chief clerk of the rear-army bureau in Fen province and Administrator of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 所在以廉平著稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, he was famed for integrity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he won renown for integrity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Taichang era.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督秦雍二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、司空公、雍州刺史，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qin and Yong provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yong province, with posthumous name Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the Staff of Authority, supreme command over Qin and Yong, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yong, with the temple name Xiaomu ("Filial and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 子侃，字伯欣，襲。

translations.literal: His son Kan, styled Boxin, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan, styled Boxin, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除南秦州長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Administrator of Southern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief administrator of Southern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、涼州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given General Who Assists the State and Governor of Liang province, with posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Governor of Liang, with the temple name Xuan ("Proclaiming").

sentences.zh: 子紹，字廣祖，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shao, styled Guangzu, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, styled Guangzu, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 興和初，征虜將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xinghe era he was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Cang province.

sentences.zh: 侃弟騰，字伏興。

translations.literal: Kan's younger brother Teng, styled Fuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's younger brother Teng, whose style name was Fuxing.

sentences.zh: 卒於安東將軍、光州刺史、襄城縣開國公。

translations.literal: He died while holding the posts of General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Guang province, and founding Duke of Xiangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Guang province, and founding Duke of Xiangcheng county.

sentences.zh: 子陟，字祖遷。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, whose style name was Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 司空中郎、太尉主簿。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Ministry of Works and Chief Clerk of the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman in the Ministry of Works and chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 陟弟憬，通直郎。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Jing was Direct-access Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Jing was Direct-access Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 憬弟翽，襲父爵。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Hui inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Hui inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 騰弟隆之，武定末，太保、尚書令、平原郡開國公。

translations.literal: Teng's younger brother Longzhi, at the end of Wuding: Grand Preceptor, Director of the Masters of Writing, and founding Duke of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's younger brother Longzhi, at the end of Wuding, was Grand Preceptor, Director of the Masters of Writing, and founding Duke of Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 崔逞，字叔祖，清河東武城人也，魏中尉琰之六世孫。

translations.literal: Cui Cheng, styled Shuzu, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, sixth-generation descendant of Cui Yan, Commandant of the Heir Apparent under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cheng, whose style name was Shuzu, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery and was a sixth-generation descendant of Cui Yan, Commandant of the Heir Apparent in Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諒，晉中書令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Liang was Director of the Secretariat under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Liang had served the Jin as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖遇，仕石虎，為特進。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu served Shi Hu and was Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served Shi Hu of Later Zhao as Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 父瑜，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Yu was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 逞少好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Cheng from youth loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cheng loved learning and showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，孤貧，躬耕于野，而講誦不廢。

translations.literal: He met with disorder, was orphaned and poor, personally plowed in the fields, yet lecturing and recitation did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in the chaos of the times, orphaned and destitute, he plowed the fields with his own hands yet never abandoned his lectures and recitation.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐時，郡舉上計掾，補著作郎，撰燕記。

translations.literal: In Murong Wei's time the commandery recommended him as Clerk for the Annual Account, he was appointed Gentleman for Compilation, and compiled the Record of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Wei the commandery recommended him as clerk for the annual account; he was appointed Gentleman for Compilation and compiled the Record of Yan.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅并慕容暐，以為齊郡太守。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian annexed Murong Wei, he was made Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian conquered Murong Wei, Cheng was appointed Administrator of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，司馬昌明以逞為清河、平原二郡太守。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, Sima Changming made Cheng Administrator of both Qinghe and Pingyuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat, Sima Changming appointed Cheng administrator of both Qinghe and Pingyuan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 為翟遼所虜，授以中書令。

translations.literal: He was captured by Zhai Liao and given the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Captured by Zhai Liao, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂滅翟釗，以為祕書監。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, Cheng was made Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶東走和龍，為留臺吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, he was Minister of Personnel at the rear capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, Cheng served as Minister of Personnel at the rear capital.

sentences.zh: 及慕容驎立，逞攜妻子亡歸太祖。

translations.literal: When Murong Lin was established, Cheng took wife and children and fled to submit to the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Lin succeeded to the throne, Cheng fled with his wife and children to defect to Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 張袞先稱美逞，及見，禮遇甚重。

translations.literal: Zhang Gun had first praised Cheng; when he was seen, the courtesy shown was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun had spoken highly of Cheng beforehand; when they met, the emperor received him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 拜為尚書，任以政事，錄三十六曹，別給吏屬，居門下省。

translations.literal: He was appointed to the Masters of Writing, entrusted with government affairs, recorded the thirty-six bureaus, was separately given clerical staff, and dwelt in the Gate-Down Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Masters of Writing, entrusted with state affairs, placed in charge of all thirty-six bureaus with a separate staff of clerks, and lodged in the Gate-Down Office.

sentences.zh: 尋除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Imperial Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻中山未克，六軍乏糧，民多匿穀，問羣臣以取粟方略。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor attacked Zhongshan but did not take it; the six armies lacked grain and the people widely hid grain; he asked the ministers for a strategy to obtain grain.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Taizu besieged Zhongshan without success, the six armies ran short of grain and the people hoarded their stores; he asked his ministers for a plan to obtain supplies.

sentences.zh: 逞曰：「取椹可以助糧。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Taking mulberries can supplement grain.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Mulberries can supplement the grain supply.

sentences.zh: 故飛鴞食椹而改音，詩稱其事。

translations.literal: Hence the flying owl eats mulberries and changes its cry—the Odes praise this matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes tell how the flying owl, eating mulberries, changes its cry—that is the precedent.

sentences.zh: 」太祖雖銜其侮慢，然兵既須食，乃聽以椹當租。

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor, though he harbored resentment at the insult, yet since the army needed food, permitted mulberries to substitute for tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor resented the insolence, but with the army starving he allowed mulberries to be accepted in lieu of tax grain.

sentences.zh: 逞又曰：「可使軍人及時自取，過時則落盡。

translations.literal: Cheng also said: "One can have the soldiers gather them in season themselves; past the season they will all fall.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng added, "Let the soldiers gather them in season themselves—after the season they will all have fallen.

sentences.zh: 」太祖怒曰：「內賊未平，兵人安可解甲仗入林野而收椹乎？

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor angrily said: "Inner rebels are not yet pacified—how can soldiers lay aside armor and weapons and enter woods and fields to gather mulberries?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thundered, "The rebels within are not yet crushed—how can soldiers lay down arms and wander the woods gathering mulberries?

sentences.zh: 是何言歟！

translations.literal: What sort of talk is this!
translations.idiomatic: What kind of counsel is that!

sentences.zh: 」以中山未拔，故不加罪。

translations.literal: " Because Zhongshan was not yet taken, he did not add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Zhongshan had not yet fallen, he did not punish him—yet.

sentences.zh: 天興初，姚興侵司馬德宗襄陽戍，戍將郗恢馳使乞師於常山王遵，遵以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, Yao Xing invaded Sima Degong's garrison at Xiangyang; the garrison commander Xi Hui sent a rapid envoy begging troops from the Prince of Changshan, Zun, and Zun reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianxing, Yao Xing attacked the Jin garrison at Xiangyang under Sima Degong; the commander Xi Hui sent an urgent plea for reinforcements to the Prince of Changshan, Tuoba Zun, who reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔逞與張袞為遵書以答。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor ordered Cheng and Zhang Gun to draft Zun's reply letter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu ordered Cheng and Zhang Gun to draft the reply for Zun.

sentences.zh: 初，恢與遵書云：「賢兄虎步中原」，太祖以言悖君臣之體，敕逞、袞亦貶其主號以報之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Hui's letter to Zun it said, "Your worthy elder brother strides like a tiger across the Central Plains"; the Taizu Emperor held the words contrary to the form of ruler and minister and ordered Cheng and Gun also to demote their lord's title in the reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Hui's letter to Zun had called the Jin ruler Zun's "worthy elder brother" who "strides like a tiger across the Central Plains." The emperor judged this a breach of the proper form between sovereign and subject and ordered Cheng and Gun to demote the Jin ruler's title in the reply.

sentences.zh: 逞、袞乃云「貴主」。

translations.literal: Cheng and Gun then wrote "your honored lord."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Gun wrote instead of "your honored lord."

sentences.zh: 太祖怒曰：「使汝貶其主以答，乃稱貴主，何若賢兄也！

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor angrily said: "I ordered you to demote their lord in the reply, yet you call him 'honored lord'—how is that better than 'worthy elder brother'!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "I told you to demote their sovereign in the reply, and you write 'honored lord'—how is that better than 'worthy elder brother'?

sentences.zh: 」遂賜死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 後司馬德宗荊州刺史司馬休之等數十人為桓玄所逐，皆將來奔，至陳留南，分為二輩：一奔長安，一歸廣固。

translations.literal: Later Sima Degong's Governor of Jing province Sima Xiuzhi and several dozen others were driven out by Huan Xuan; all were about to come and submit; reaching south of Chenliu they split into two groups: one fled to Chang'an, one returned to Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Later dozens of Jin officials led by Sima Xiuzhi, Governor of Jing province under Sima Degong, were driven out by Huan Xuan and set out to defect to Wei. South of Chenliu they divided: one party went to Chang'an, the other to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 太祖初聞休之等降，大悅，後怪其不至，詔兗州尋訪，獲其從者，問故，皆曰：「國家威聲遠被，是以休之等咸欲歸闕，及聞崔逞被殺，故奔二處。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor at first heard that Xiuzhi and others were submitting and was greatly pleased; later he wondered that they had not arrived, ordered Yan province to search, seized their followers, and asked the reason; all said: "The state's awesome reputation reaches far, so Xiuzhi and others all wished to return to the court; when they heard Cui Cheng was killed, they therefore fled to the two places.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor rejoiced to hear that Xiuzhi and his party were coming; when they failed to arrive he ordered a search in Yan province and questioned their attendants. All gave the same answer: "Your Majesty's renown reaches far, and every man among us wished to submit—until we heard that Cui Cheng had been executed; then we fled in two directions.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深悔之。

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 自是士人有過者，多見優容。

translations.literal: From this time, when scholars had faults they were mostly treated with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: After that, when scholars at court erred, the emperor usually showed forbearance.

sentences.zh: 逞七子，二子早亡，第三子義，義弟諲，諲弟禕，禕弟嚴，嚴弟賾。

translations.literal: Cheng had seven sons; two sons died young; the third son Yi; Yi's younger brother Shen; Shen's younger brother Yi; Yi's younger brother Yan; Yan's younger brother Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had seven sons, of whom two died young. The five who survived were, from the third son on: Yi, then Shen, Yi, Yan, and Ze, each the next younger brother in turn.

sentences.zh: [11]逞之內徙也，終慮不免，乃使其妻張氏與四子留冀州，令歸慕容德，遂奔廣固。

translations.literal: [11] When Cheng was moved inward he ultimately feared he would not escape harm, so he made his wife Lady Zhang and four sons remain in Ji province, ordered them to submit to Murong De, and himself fled to Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: [11] When Cheng was transferred to the inner domains he feared he would not survive, sent his wife Lady Zhang and four sons back to Ji province to submit to Murong De, and himself fled to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 逞獨與小子賾在平城。

translations.literal: Cheng alone with his youngest son Ze was at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng remained at Pingcheng with only his youngest son Ze.

sentences.zh: 及逞之死，亦以此為譴。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, this too was made a ground of reproach.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng was executed, this abandonment of his family was counted among his offenses.

sentences.zh: 賾，字泰沖。

translations.literal: Ze, styled Taichong.
translations.idiomatic: Ze, whose style name was Taichong.

sentences.zh: 初為太子洗馬，後稍遷散騎常侍，[12]賜爵清河侯，後世祖聞劉義隆以諲為冀州刺史，乃曰：「義隆知用其兄，我豈無冀州也。

translations.literal: He was first Preceptor of the Heir Apparent's Household, later gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, [12] enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe; later Emperor Shizu heard that Liu Yilong had made Shen Governor of Ji province and said: "Yilong knows how to use his elder brother—do I lack a man for Ji province?
translations.idiomatic: He began as preceptor in the heir apparent's household, rose to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, [12] and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe. When Emperor Shizu heard that Liu Yilong of Song had appointed Shen governor of Ji, he said, "Yilong knows how to use an elder brother—shall I have no governor for Ji?

sentences.zh: 」乃以賾為平東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ze was made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon appointed Ze General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 又為大鴻臚，持節策拜楊難當為南秦王。

translations.literal: He was also made Grand Herald, and bearing the staff invested Yang Nan Dang as King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Grand Herald and, bearing the imperial staff, invested Yang Nan Dang as King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 奉使數返，光揚朝命，世祖善之。

translations.literal: On missions he returned many times, spreading and glorifying the court's commands; Emperor Shizu was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated embassies he carried the court's authority abroad, and Emperor Shizu approved.

sentences.zh: 及驃騎大將軍、樂平王丕等督諸軍取上邽，使賾齎詔於丕前喻難當奉詔。

translations.literal: When Grand General Who Quells Speed, Prince of Leping Pi and others directed the various armies to take Shanggui, Ze was sent bearing the edict before Pi to explain to Nan Dang that he should comply with the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Who Quells Speed, the Prince of Leping Pi, and others commanded the armies to seize Shanggui, Ze was dispatched with an imperial edict to Pi's camp to instruct Nan Dang to submit.

sentences.zh: 後與方士韋文秀詣王屋山造金丹，不就。

translations.literal: Later, together with the adept Wei Wenxiu he went to Mount Wangwu to make the golden elixir, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the adept Wei Wenxiu on Mount Wangwu to seek the golden elixir, but failed.

sentences.zh: 真君初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 賾五子。

translations.literal: Ze—five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Ze fathered five sons.

sentences.zh: 長子秉，字公禮。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Bing, styled Gongli.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bing, whose style name was Gongli.

sentences.zh: 早終，無子。

translations.literal: He died young; he had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Bing died early and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 秉弟廣，字公淵，襲爵。

translations.literal: Bing's younger brother Guang, styled Gongyuan, inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's younger brother Guang, styled Gongyuan, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 拜平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 子法度，早終。

translations.literal: His son Fadu died young.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son Fadu also died young.

sentences.zh: 廣弟軌，字公則。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Gui, styled Gongze.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Gui, whose style name was Gongze.

sentences.zh: 太子中舍人、鎮南司馬。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Administrator of the Army That Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant in the heir apparent's household and as chief administrator on the staff of the Army That Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 軌弟穆，字公和。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Mu, styled Gonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Mu, whose style name was Gonghe.

sentences.zh: 早終。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: Mu too died early.

sentences.zh: 穆弟叡，字哲，小字男季。

translations.literal: Mu's younger brother Rui, styled Zhe, pet name Nanji.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's younger brother Rui, styled Zhe and known in youth as Nanji.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，以交通境外伏誅。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozong's reign, for communicating with foreign lands he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was put to death for dealings across the border.

sentences.zh: 從兄景真以子思叔繼叡。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Jingzhen made his son Sishu succeed Rui.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Jingzhen had his son Sishu adopted to continue Rui's line.

sentences.zh: 思叔，少為中書學生，遷中書博士。

translations.literal: Sishu in youth was a student of the Secretariat Academy, and was promoted to Secretariat Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Sishu began as a student in the Secretariat Academy and rose to Secretariat Erudite.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，歷上黨，鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he successively served as Governor of Shangdang and Governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he held the governorships of Shangdang and Julu in succession.

sentences.zh: 自逞之死至叡之誅，三世積五十餘年而在北一門盡矣。

translations.literal: From Cheng's death to Rui's execution, three generations accumulating more than fifty years—and the northern branch of the house was ended.
translations.idiomatic: From Cheng's execution to Rui's, three generations and more than fifty years passed, and the northern line of the family was utterly extinguished.

sentences.zh: 初，三齊平，禕孫相如入國，以才學知名。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when the Three Qi were pacified, Yi's grandson Xiangru entered the state and was known for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Qi were conquered, Yi's grandson Xiangru came to Wei and won renown for scholarly talent.

sentences.zh: 舉冀州秀才，早卒。

translations.literal: He was nominated Provincial Candidate of Ji province and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial candidate from Ji, he died young.

sentences.zh: 相如弟彧，在術藝傳。

translations.literal: Xiangru's younger brother Yu—he is in the Treatise on Technical Arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru's younger brother Yu has his biography in the Treatise on Technical Arts.

sentences.zh: 逞兄適，[13]字寧祖，亦有名於時。

translations.literal: Cheng's elder brother Shi, [13] styled Ningzu, was also famed in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's elder brother Shi, [13] whose style name was Ningzu, was likewise noted in his time.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂尚書左丞，范陽、昌黎二郡太守。

translations.literal: Under Murong Chui he was Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing; he was Governor of Fanyang and Governor of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing and later as governor of Fanyang and Changli.

sentences.zh: 適曾孫延壽，冀州主簿。

translations.literal: Shi's great-grandson Yanshou was Chief Recorder of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's great-grandson Yanshou served as chief recorder of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，甚收鄉曲之譽。

translations.literal: Light with wealth and fond of giving, he greatly earned praise among the people of his district.
translations.idiomatic: He spent freely and gave generously, and won wide praise in his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 延壽子隆宗，簡率愛友，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yanshou's son Longzong was plain and straightforward, loving toward friends and companions; his mourning conduct was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou's son Longzong was openhearted and devoted to his friends; his filial conduct in mourning was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 歷位冀州別駕，蘭陵、燕郡二郡太守，司空諮議參軍，冀州中正，中軍大將軍府長史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Ji province Personal Assistant, Governor of Lanling and Governor of Yanyun, Staff Officer for Consultation under the Minister of Works, Rectifier of Ji province, and Chief Administrator on the staff of the Grand General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of personal assistant in Ji, governor of Lanling and Yanyun, consultative staff officer under the Minister of Works, Ji rectifier, and chief administrator on the staff of the Grand General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 仁信待物，出於至誠，故見重於世。

translations.literal: He treated others with humaneness and trust, from utmost sincerity; therefore he was valued by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Humane and trustworthy to the depth of sincerity itself, he was held in high esteem by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈前將軍。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Governor of Qi; his posthumous name was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Governor of Qi, with the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子敬保，員外散騎侍郎、冀州儀同府從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son Jingbao was Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Attendant on the staff of the Yitong office of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingbao served as Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and as staff attendant in the Ji Yitong office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 子子恒，官至征虜將軍、魯郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Ziheng reached the posts of General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziheng rose to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: Ziheng also died early.

sentences.zh: 子恒弟子安，冠軍將軍、西兗州司馬。

translations.literal: Ziheng's younger brother's son Zi'an was General Who Establishes Might and Chief Administrator of Western Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Ziheng's brother's son Zi'an served as General Who Establishes Might and chief administrator of Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 子安弟子昇，開府參軍。

translations.literal: Zi'an's younger brother's son Zisheng was a Staff Officer on a general's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'an's brother's son Zisheng served as a staff officer on a general's establishment.

sentences.zh: 武定中，坐連元瑾事，兄弟並伏法。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, implicated in the affair connected with Yuan Jin, the brothers were all executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding they were executed along with their brothers in the affair tied to Yuan Jin.

sentences.zh: 封懿，字處德，勃海蓨人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yi, styled Chude, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi, whose style name was Chude, was from Tiao in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖釋，晉東夷校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shi was Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shi had been Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 父放，慕容暐吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fang served Murong Wei as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 兄孚，慕容超太尉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Fu was Grand Marshal under Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Fu served Murong Chao as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 懿儁偉有才氣，能屬文，與孚雖器行有長短，然名位略齊。

translations.literal: Yi was handsome and imposing, with talent and spirit, able to compose prose; with Fu, though their capacity and conduct had strengths and weaknesses, their fame and rank were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a striking figure of talent who could write well; he and Fu differed in stature and character, yet their renown and rank were much the same.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容寶，位至中書令、民部尚書。

translations.literal: He served Murong Bao and reached the posts of Central Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Bao as Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 寶敗，歸闕，除給事黃門侍郎、都坐大官、寧朔將軍、章安子。

translations.literal: When Bao was defeated he returned to the court and was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat, General Who Pacifies the North, and Viscount of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao fell he submitted to Wei and was made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master of the Imperial Commissariat, General Who Pacifies the North, and Viscount of Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 太祖數引見，問以慕容舊事。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu repeatedly summoned him to audience and questioned him about old Yan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu often received him and asked about the former Yan court.

sentences.zh: 懿應對疏慢，廢還家。

translations.literal: Yi's replies were negligent and disrespectful; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered with careless disrespect and was dismissed to his home.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，復徵拜都坐大官，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Taizong's reign he was again summoned and appointed Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat, and advanced in noble rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Taizong's reign he was recalled as Grand Master of the Imperial Commissariat and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Taichang era.

sentences.zh: 懿撰燕書，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Yi compiled the Book of Yan, which circulated quite widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote the Book of Yan, which enjoyed wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 子玄之，坐與司馬國璠、溫楷等謀亂，伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Xuanzhi, for sitting in a plot for disorder with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanzhi was executed for plotting rebellion with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，太宗謂之曰：「終不令絕汝種也，將宥爾一子。

translations.literal: At the execution Emperor Taizong said to him: "In the end I shall not let your seed be cut off; I shall pardon one of your sons.
translations.idiomatic: At execution Emperor Taizong told him, "I will not end your line; I shall spare one of your sons.

sentences.zh: 」玄之請曰：「弟虔之子磨奴，字君明，早孤，乞全其命。

translations.literal: " Xuanzhi requested saying: "My younger brother Qian's son Monu, styled Junming, was orphaned early—I beg that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzhi pleaded, "Spare my nephew Monu, styled Junming, Qian's orphaned son.

sentences.zh: 」乃殺玄之四子，而赦磨奴。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they killed Xuanzhi's four sons and pardoned Monu.
translations.idiomatic: " They killed Xuanzhi's four sons and pardoned Monu.

sentences.zh: 磨奴被刑為宦人。

translations.literal: Monu suffered punishment and became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Monu was castrated and made a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 崔浩之誅也，世祖謂磨奴曰：「汝本應全，所以致刑者，事由浩之故。

translations.literal: At Cui Hao's execution Emperor Shizu said to Monu: "You should originally have been entirely spared; the reason you suffered punishment was because of Hao's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao fell, Emperor Shizu told Monu, "You should have been spared entirely; it was Hao's affair that brought your punishment.

sentences.zh: 」後為中曹監，西使張掖，賜爵富城子，加建威將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: " Later he was made Director of the Middle Palace Attendants, sent as envoy to the west to Zhangye, granted the noble rank Viscount of Fucheng, and additionally made General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He later became Director of the Middle Palace Attendants, was sent west to Zhangye, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fucheng, and was further made General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為冠軍將軍、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Huai province.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was sent out as General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Huai.

sentences.zh: 太和七年卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、冀州刺史、勃海公，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Ji province, and Duke of Bohai, with the posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Ji, and Duke of Bohai, with posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 以族子叔念為後，高祖賜名回。

translations.literal: A clansman's son Shunian was made his heir; Emperor Gaozong granted the name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He took his clansman Shunian as heir, and Emperor Gaozong granted him the name Hui.

sentences.zh: 回父鑒，即慕容暐太尉弈之後也。

translations.literal: Hui's father Jian was a descendant of Murong Wei's Grand Marshal Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's father Jian descended from Murong Wei's Grand Marshal Yi.

sentences.zh: 回，皇興初為中書學生。

translations.literal: Hui—in the beginning of Huangxing was a student of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Huangxing, Hui enrolled as a student in the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 襲爵富城子，累遷太子家令。

translations.literal: He inherited the noble rank Viscount of Fucheng and was repeatedly promoted to Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the title of Viscount of Fucheng and rose to become Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以回行華州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Hui was put in charge of Huazhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, Hui was assigned to administer Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 回在州鞭中散大夫党智孫，為尚書左丞韋績糾奏，[14]免。

translations.literal: While in the province Hui flogged the Gentleman of Palace Attendance Dang Zhisun; he was impeached by Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing Wei Ji, [14] and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In office Hui had the Gentleman of Palace Attendance Dang Zhisun beaten; Left Assistant Wei Ji impeached him, [14] and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮遠將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of An province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of An.

sentences.zh: 山民愿朴，父子賓旅，同寢一室。
