translations.literal: The mountain people of Yuan Pu—father and son, guest and host—shared one room to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Among the mountain folk of Yuan Pu, fathers and sons, hosts and guests alike, slept in a single room.

sentences.zh: 回下車，勒令別處，其俗遂改。

translations.literal: When Hui arrived to take office he ordered them to separate quarters, and their custom was thereby changed.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Hui ordered them to lodge apart, and the custom was changed.

sentences.zh: 徵為太尉長史，頻行定州、徐州事，尋除後將軍、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Chief Administrator on the staff of the Grand Commander and repeatedly acted in the affairs of Ding and Xu provinces; soon after he was appointed Rear General and Governor of Fen province.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as chief administrator on the Grand Commander's staff, he repeatedly administered Ding and Xu; he was then made Rear General and Governor of Fen.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，轉涼州刺史，加右將軍，固辭不拜，仍授平北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Suzong's reign he was transferred to Governor of Liang province and additionally made Right General; he firmly declined to accept the appointment, and was thereupon granted General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne he was transferred to Governor of Liang with the additional rank of Right General; he firmly declined, and was instead made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 時大乘寇亂之後，加以水潦，百姓困乏。

translations.literal: At that time, after the disorders of the Mahayana sect, floods were added on top, and the common people were exhausted and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: The province had suffered Mahayana rebellion and then flood; the people were destitute.

sentences.zh: 回表求賑恤，免其兵調，州內甚賴之。

translations.literal: Hui memorialized requesting relief and succor, exemption from military levies; within the province they greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized for relief and exemption from military levies, and the province relied heavily on him.

sentences.zh: 又為度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋轉都官尚書，冀州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Minister of Justice and Great Rectifier of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Minister of Justice and Great Rectifier of Ji.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭雲諂事長秋卿劉騰，貨騰紫纈四百匹，得為安州刺史。

translations.literal: Zheng Yun of Xingyang curried favor by serving the Director of the Long Autumn Liu Teng, and with four hundred bolts of purple patterned silk bought from Teng the post of Governor of An province.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun of Xingyang fawned on Liu Teng, Director of the Long Autumn, and bought the governorship of An with four hundred bolts of purple gauze.

sentences.zh: 除書旦出，暮往詣回，坐未定，謂回曰：「我為安州，卿知之否？

translations.literal: The appointment letter came out at dawn; in the evening he went to call on Hui, and before he had settled into his seat he said to Hui: "I am made Governor of An—do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: His appointment came at dawn; that evening he called on Feng Hui and, before he had even sat down, said, "I have been made governor of An—did you know?

sentences.zh: 彼土治生，何事為便？

translations.literal: In that land, for making a living, what affair is most convenient?
translations.idiomatic: What is the best way to turn a profit in that territory?

sentences.zh: 」回答之曰：「卿荷國寵靈，位至方伯，雖不能拔園葵，去織婦，宜思方略以濟百姓，如何見造而問治生乎？

translations.literal: " Hui replied saying: "You bear the state's favor and numinous grace, your rank reaching a regional lord; although you cannot uproot the garden mallows and send away the weaving women, you ought to think of plans and strategies to aid the common people—why on your first visit come to ask about making a living?
translations.idiomatic: " Hui replied, "You bear the state's grace and hold a frontier post; though you cannot, like Gongyi Xiu of old, uproot the mallows in your garden and send away your weaving women, you should aid the people—why on your first visit ask about private profit?

sentences.zh: 封回不為商賈，何以相示。

translations.literal: Feng Hui is no merchant—how should he show you?
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui is no merchant—what counsel could I give you?

sentences.zh: 」雲慚媿失色。

translations.literal: " Yun was ashamed and abashed, losing color.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun flushed with shame and went pale.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，召百官問得失，羣臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held court and summoned the hundred officials to ask about gains and losses; the multitude of ministers did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling took the regency she asked the assembled officials what was right and wrong in government, and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 回對曰：「昔孔丘為司寇，十日而誅少正卯，魯國肅然，欺巧自息。

translations.literal: Hui replied saying: "In the past Kong Qiu served as Minister of Crime; within ten days he executed Shaozheng Mao, and Lu was solemnly ordered—deception and craft ceased of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui answered, "When Confucius was Minister of Crime he executed Shaozheng Mao within ten days, and Lu became orderly—deceit withered away.

sentences.zh: 姬旦行戮，不避兄弟，周道用隆。

translations.literal: Ji Dan carried out executions without avoiding his own brothers, and the Way of Zhou rose in prominence.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou executed kin without favor, and the Zhou dynasty flourished.

sentences.zh: 徐偃專行仁義，其國乃滅。

translations.literal: Xu Yan devoted himself exclusively to humaneness and righteousness, and his state was thereby destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan of Song relied on benevolence alone, and his state perished.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有不厲威刑而能治者。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present there has never been one who could govern without sternly enforcing punitive law.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, no ruler has governed well without stern punishments.

sentences.zh: 頃來頗由長吏寬怠，侵剝百姓，盜賊羣起。

translations.literal: Recently it has largely been because local superiors are lax and negligent, encroaching on and exploiting the common people, and bandits and thieves rise in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Lately local officials have grown lax, preyed on the people, and bandits have risen everywhere.

sentences.zh: 請肅刑書，以懲未犯。

translations.literal: I request that the penal code be made solemn and strict, to warn those who have not yet offended.
translations.idiomatic: Make the penal code strict again, to deter crime before it happens.

sentences.zh: 」太后意納之，而不能用。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager inwardly accepted it, but could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager took his counsel to heart but could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 轉為七兵尚書，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Seven Armies, concurrently holding the post of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Seven Armies and also served as Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射元欽與從父兄麗妻崔氏姦通，回乃劾奏，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Qin had illicit relations with his paternal cousin Li's wife Lady Cui; Hui thereupon impeached and memorialized, and men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Yuan Qin committed adultery with his cousin Li's wife Lady Cui, Feng Hui impeached him, and contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 除鎮東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，徵為殿中尚書，頻表遜職，以為右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Suzong's reign he was summoned as Minister in the Palace; he repeatedly memorialized declining office, and was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he was recalled as Palace Minister but repeatedly asked to retire and was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害於河陰，時年七十七。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he met with disaster at Heyin; at the time he was seventy-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed in the massacre at Heyin, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司空公、定州刺史，諡曰孝宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous name Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, and Governor of Ding, with the posthumous name Xiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 長子隆之，武定中，開府儀同三司、齊州刺史、安德郡開國公。

translations.literal: His eldest son Longzhi—in the Wuding era was Commissioner Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Governor of Qi province, and Duke of a State of Ande commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Longzhi, during Wuding, held the rank of Commissioner Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, was Governor of Qi, and was Duke of the State of Ande.

sentences.zh: 子子繪，武定中，勃海太守。

translations.literal: His son Zihui—in the Wuding era was Governor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Zihui served as Governor of Bohai during Wuding.

sentences.zh: 隆之弟興之，字祖冑。

translations.literal: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Zuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, whose style name was Zuzhou.

sentences.zh: 經明行修，恬素清靜。

translations.literal: He was clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, plain and simple, quiet and serene.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the classics and upright in conduct, living plainly and in quiet seclusion.

sentences.zh: 起家太學博士，員外郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and External Section Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and External Section Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為瀛冀二州平北府長史，所歷有當官之譽。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters of Ying and Ji provinces; in every post he held he had the reputation of a proper official.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief administrator of the Pacify-the-North headquarters for Ying and Ji provinces, earning a reputation in every office for discharging his duties well.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中卒。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xiaochang era.

sentences.zh: 天平中，追贈散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was posthumously given Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianping he was posthumously made Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 尋重贈殿中尚書，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Soon he was again posthumously given Minister in the Palace, with the posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received a further posthumous appointment as Minister in the Palace, with the posthumous name Wen.

translations.literal: Editorial annotation marker [15].
translations.idiomatic: [15] Textual note: various editions read the posthumous name as Xiao rather than Wen; the Bei and Dian versions, the History of the Northern Dynasties, and the Tang genealogical tables all have Wen. The character Xiao here is likely a displaced character from the following line naming Xiaowan; the text follows the Bei and Dian versions.

sentences.zh: 子孝琬，字子倩。

translations.literal: His son Xiaowan, styled Ziqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaowan, whose style name was Ziqian.

sentences.zh: [16]武定末，開府中郎。

translations.literal: [16] Late in the Wuding era, Attendant in the General's Staff.
translations.idiomatic: [16] In the closing years of Wuding he served as Attendant in the General's Staff.

sentences.zh: 孝琬弟孝琰，祕書郎。

translations.literal: Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan, Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan was a Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 興之弟延之，字祖業。

translations.literal: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, whose style name was Zuye.

sentences.zh: 天平中，驃騎大將軍、青州刺史、[17]剡縣開國子。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Qing province, [17] and Viscount of a State of Shan county.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he held the titles of Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Qing, [17] and Viscount of Shan county.

sentences.zh: 磨奴既以回為後，請於顯祖，贈鑒寧遠將軍、滄水太守。

translations.literal: Monu, having already taken Hui as his heir, requested of Emperor Xianzu that Jian be posthumously given General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: After Monu had adopted Hui as his heir, he asked Emperor Xianzu to posthumously grant Jian the rank of General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 鑒長子琳，字彥寶。

translations.literal: Jian's eldest son Lin, styled Yanbao.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's eldest son Lin, whose style name was Yanbao.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末，本州表貢，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Xianzu's reign, the province recommended him as tribute; he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xianzu's reign the province submitted him as tribute, and he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，大軍南討，琳參鎮南軍事。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozong's reign, when the great army marched south to chastise, Lin served as staff officer for the Pacify-the-South campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Gaozong's reign, when the main force marched south on campaign, Lin served on the Pacify-the-South staff.

sentences.zh: 後為河南七州大使。

translations.literal: Later he became Envoy of the Seven Provinces of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as envoy to the seven Henan provinces.

sentences.zh: 還，拜中書侍郎，與侍中、南平王馮誕等議定律令，賜布帛六百匹、粟六百石、馬牛各一。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Gentleman in Attendance at the Secretariat; together with Palace Attendant and Prince of Nanping Feng Dan and others he deliberated on statutes and ordinances, and was granted six hundred bolts of cloth and silk, six hundred shi of grain, and one horse and one ox each.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he was made Gentleman in Attendance at the Secretariat and, with Palace Attendant Feng Dan, Prince of Nanping, and others, helped revise the laws and ordinances; he received six hundred bolts of cloth and silk, six hundred shi of grain, and one horse and one ox.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉長史，轉司宗下大夫，有長者之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Administrator on the Grand Commander's staff, then to Lower Grand Master of the Director of Clans, and had the reputation of an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief administrator on the Grand Commander's staff, then to Lower Grand Master in the Directorate of Clans, and was known as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 行東兗州事。

translations.literal: He administered the affairs of Eastern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to administer Eastern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 及改定百官，除司空長史。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were reformed and fixed, he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaucracy was reorganized, he was made chief administrator to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為立忠將軍、南青州刺史、兼散騎常侍、持節、西道大使。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Loyalty, Governor of Southern Qing province, concurrently Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, Bearer of the Staff, and Envoy of the Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Southern Qing, also serving as Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, Bearer of the Staff, and envoy to the western circuit.

sentences.zh: 還為長兼太中大夫，轉廣平內史，又為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On returning he served as Senior Concurrent Grand Master of the Palace, then as Internal Administrator of Guangping, and again as Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he held the concurrent post of Senior Grand Master of the Palace, then became Internal Administrator of Guangping, and afterward Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，除後將軍、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Shizong's reign he was appointed Rear General and Governor of Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made Rear General and Governor of Xia.

sentences.zh: 徵為安東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Shengui era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Shengui era.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、撫軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the titles Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子元稱，元稱弟子盛，並早卒。

translations.literal: His son Yuancheng, and Yuancheng's younger brother's son Sheng, both died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuancheng and Yuancheng's nephew Sheng both died early.

sentences.zh: 子盛弟子施，武定末，沛郡太守。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother's son Shi—in the closing years of Wuding was Administrator of Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's nephew Shi served as Administrator of Pei commandery in the closing years of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 琳子肅，在文苑傳。

translations.literal: Lin's son Su—he is in the Treatise on Literary Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's son Su has his biography in the Treatise on Literary Masters.

sentences.zh: 懿從兄子愷，字思悌，弈之孫也。

translations.literal: Yi's paternal cousin's son Kai, styled Sibian, was a grandson of Murong Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi's cousin Kai, whose style name was Sibian, was a grandson of Murong Yi.

sentences.zh: 父勸，慕容垂侍中、太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had served Murong Chui as Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 愷，給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Kai—Attendant in Attendance at the Yellow Gate, Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kai held the posts of Attendant in Attendance at the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後入代都，名出懿子玄之右，俱坐司馬氏事死。

translations.literal: Later he entered the capital at Dai, and his fame surpassed that of Yi's son Xuanzhi; both were executed on account of the Sima affair.
translations.idiomatic: He later came to the capital at Dai, where his reputation outshone that of Yi's son Xuanzhi; both men were put to death in the Sima affair.

sentences.zh: 愷妻，盧玄姊也。

translations.literal: Kai's wife was an elder sister of Lu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's wife was the elder sister of Lu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 愷子伯達棄母及妻李氏南奔河表，改婚房氏。

translations.literal: Kai's son Boda abandoned his mother and his wife Lady Li and fled south to the south of the Yellow River, remarrying into the Fang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Boda deserted his mother and his wife Lady Li and fled south of the Yellow River, taking a new wife from the Fang clan.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末，伯達子休傑內入，祖母盧猶存，垂百歲矣，而李已死。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Xianzu's reign, Boda's son Xiujie entered within the borders; his grandmother Lady Lu was still alive, nearly a hundred years old, while Li had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xianzu's reign, Boda's son Xiujie returned to the north; his grandmother Lady Lu was still living, close to a hundred years old, though Lady Li was already dead.

sentences.zh: 休傑，高祖時以歸國勳為河間太守，兼冀州咸陽王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Xiujie—in Emperor Gaozong's time, for merit in returning to the realm was made Administrator of Hejian and concurrently Advisory Assistant in the Xianyang Princedom of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujie, rewarded under Emperor Gaozong for returning to the dynasty, became Administrator of Hejian and concurrently advisory assistant in the Xianyang princedom of Ji.

sentences.zh: 休傑從弟靈祐，仕劉義隆為青州治中、勃海太守。

translations.literal: Xiujie's younger cousin Lingyou served Liu Yilong as Administrator-in-Chief of Qing province and Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujie's cousin Lingyou served under Liu Yilong as Administrator-in-Chief of Qing and Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜平三齊，靈祐率二百人詣白曜降，賜爵下密子。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao pacified the Three Qi, Lingyou led two hundred men to Baiyao to surrender and was granted the title Viscount of Xiami.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Baiyao conquered the Three Qi, Lingyou brought two hundred men to Baiyao to submit; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiami.

sentences.zh: 後除建威將軍、勃海太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: At that he died.

sentences.zh: 子進壽，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jinshou succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinshou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為揚州治中，以失義州為刺史元志所殺。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time he was Administrator-in-Chief of Yang province and was killed by Governor Yuan Zhi for losing Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as Administrator-in-Chief of Yang and was slain by Governor Yuan Zhi after losing Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 事具志傳。

translations.literal: The affair is fully set forth in Zhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Yuan Zhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 子子游，武定中，開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Ziyou—in the Wuding era was Central Army Adjutant in the General's Staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyou served during Wuding as Central Army Adjutant in the General's Staff.

sentences.zh: 進壽弟蚌，卒於冀州別駕。

translations.literal: Jinshou's younger brother Bang died while Administrator-in-Chief of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshou's younger brother Bang died in office as Administrator-in-Chief of Ji.

sentences.zh: 蚌弟粲，起家荊州長流參軍。

translations.literal: Bang's younger brother Can began his career as Long-term Staff Officer in Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Bang's younger brother Can entered service as Long-term Staff Officer in Jing province.

sentences.zh: 司空水曹參軍、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Staff Officer in the Water Bureau of the Minister of Works, Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer in the Water Bureau of the Minister of Works and as Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷征東將軍、廣州長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General Who Campaigns East and Chief Administrator of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to General Who Campaigns East and chief administrator of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 還，除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈衞將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General of the Guard and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Guard and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 回族叔軌，字廣度。

translations.literal: Feng Hui's clansman Gui, styled Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui's clansman Gui, whose style name was Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 沉謹好學，博通經傳。

translations.literal: Deeply cautious and fond of learning, he was broadly versed in the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and studious, he mastered the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 與光祿大夫武邑孫惠蔚同志友善，惠蔚每推軌曰：「封生之於經義，非但章句可奇，其標明綱格，統括大歸，吾所弗如者多矣。

translations.literal: He shared the same aims and friendship with Sun Huiwei, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue of Wuyi; Huiwei would always commend Gui, saying: "Master Feng's grasp of the meaning of the classics is remarkable not only in glossing the lines; in clarifying the framework and summing up the great import, there is much in which I am not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: He was of one mind and close friends with Sun Huiwei, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue of Wuyi. Huiwei often praised Gui, saying, "In classical learning Master Feng is extraordinary not merely in parsing the text; in setting out the governing principles and gathering up the larger meaning, I am his inferior in many respects.

sentences.zh: 」善自修潔，儀容甚偉。

translations.literal: He was good at cultivating himself and keeping clean; his bearing and appearance were very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He took care in grooming himself, and his presence was striking.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「學士不事修飾，此賢何獨如此？

translations.literal: Someone said: "Scholars do not trouble themselves with adornment—why is this worthy alone like this?
translations.idiomatic: Someone remarked, "Men of learning do not fuss over their appearance—why does this worthy alone do so?

sentences.zh: 」軌聞，笑曰：「君子整其衣冠，尊其瞻視，何必蓬頭垢面，然後為賢。

translations.literal: When Gui heard it he laughed and said: "The gentleman sets his cap and robes in order and holds his gaze with dignity—why must he be unkempt and filthy before he counts as worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Gui smiled and said, "A gentleman orders his dress and holds himself with dignity in the eyes of others—must one be disheveled and dirty to be called worthy?

sentences.zh: 」言者慚退。

translations.literal: The speaker withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The critic withdrew, abashed.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜著作佐郎，稍遷尚書儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Composition, and was gradually promoted to Director in the Ceremonials Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was made Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and gradually rose to Director in the Ceremonials Section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 兼員外散騎常侍，銜命高麗。

translations.literal: Concurrently Acting Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, he bore the imperial command to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Also serving as Acting Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, he carried an imperial mission to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 高麗王雲恃其偏遠，稱疾不親受詔。

translations.literal: King Yun of Goguryeo, relying on his remoteness, claimed illness and would not receive the edict in person.
translations.idiomatic: King Yun of Goguryeo, trusting in his distance from the court, pleaded illness and refused to receive the edict in person.

sentences.zh: 軌正色詰之，喻以大義，雲乃北面受詔。

translations.literal: Gui sternly questioned him, expounded the great principle, and Yun then turned north to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Gui questioned him with stern countenance, set forth the larger principle, and Yun at last turned north to accept the edict.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹虜掠邊民六十餘口，又為高麗擁掠東歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan had raided and carried off more than sixty border people, who were then seized again by Goguryeo on their way east.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Khitan had raided the frontier and taken more than sixty subjects captive; Goguryeo had then seized them again as they traveled eastward.

sentences.zh: 軌具聞其狀，移書徵之，雲悉資給遣還。

translations.literal: Gui fully learned the circumstances, sent a written summons, and Yun fully supplied provisions and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Gui learned the full circumstances, sent a formal demand, and Yun furnished supplies and sent every captive home.

sentences.zh: 有司奏軌遠使絕域，不辱朝命，權宜曉慰，邊民來蘇，宜加爵賞。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Gui, on a distant mission to a remote region, had not disgraced the court's command; by timely expedients he had reassured the people and the border folk had revived—rank and reward were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported that on a distant mission to a far country Gui had upheld the imperial charge; by prudent measures he had reassured the people and restored life on the frontier, and merited promotion and reward.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔曰：「權宜徵口，使人常體，但光揚有稱，宜賞一階。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's edict said: "Expedient recovery of captives is the constant duty of envoys, but since he has won praise for spreading glory abroad, one rank of reward is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong decreed, "Recovering captives by expedient means is an envoy's ordinary duty, yet because he has won repute for bringing honor to the court, he should receive one step of promotion.

sentences.zh: 」轉考功郎中，除本郡中正。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Merit Examinations and appointed Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He was moved to Director in the Bureau of Merit Examinations and made Rectifier of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 勃海太守崔休入為吏部郎，以兄考事干軌。

translations.literal: Cui Xiu, Administrator of Bohai, entered service as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and sought Gui's favor regarding his elder brother's merit examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiu, Administrator of Bohai, came in as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and tried to influence Gui over his elder brother's merit review.

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「法者，天下之平，不可以舊君故虧之也。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Law is the balance of the realm—it cannot be bent because of a former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied, "Law is the scale of the empire; it cannot be compromised for the sake of a former superior.

sentences.zh: 」休歎其守正。

translations.literal: " Xiu sighed at his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 軌在臺中，稱為儒雅。

translations.literal: While Gui was in the Secretariat he was called a man of refined learning.
translations.idiomatic: At the Secretariat Gui was regarded as a scholar of refinement.

sentences.zh: 奏請遣四門博士明經學者，檢試諸州學生。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Erudites of the Four Gates who were versed in the classics be sent to examine students in the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking that Four Gates Erudites learned in the classics be dispatched to test provincial students.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋除國子博士，加揚武將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University and given the additional rank of General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Erudite of the Imperial University with the additional title General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 假通直散騎常侍，慰勞汾州山胡。

translations.literal: Acting Direct-and-Upright Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, he went to comfort and reassure the Mountain Hu of Fen province.
translations.idiomatic: As Acting Direct-and-Upright Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, he was sent to comfort the Mountain Hu of Fen province.

sentences.zh: 司空、清河王懌表修明堂辟雍，詔百僚集議。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi, memorialized on repairing the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy; an edict ordered the hundred officials to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, memorialized for the repair of the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy, and the court ordered the officials to meet in consultation.

sentences.zh: 軌議曰：「明堂者，布政之宮，在國之陽，所以嚴父配天，聽朔設教，其經構之式，蓋已尚矣。

translations.literal: Gui argued: "The Bright Hall is the palace of issuing government; it stands in the yang of the state, where one honors the father and matches Heaven, listens to the new moon, and establishes instruction—the pattern of its construction has long been exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui argued, "The Bright Hall is the hall of governance, set in the state's southern aspect, where the ruler honors his father and joins Heaven, proclaims the new moon, and establishes teaching; the form of its construction has been revered since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 故周官匠人職云：夏后氏世室，殷人重屋，周人明堂，五室、九階、四戶、八窗。

translations.literal: Thus the Craftsman in the Offices of Zhou says: the Hall of the Xia, the Double-eaved Hall of the Yin, the Bright Hall of the Zhou—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, eight windows.
translations.idiomatic: The Craftsman's Office in the Rites of Zhou records: the Hall of the Xia, the Double-eaved Hall of the Yin, the Bright Hall of the Zhou—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, and eight windows.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：『或舉宗廟，或舉王寢，或舉明堂，互之以見同制。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: 'Sometimes the ancestral temple is cited, sometimes the royal bedchamber, sometimes the Bright Hall—by citing them interchangeably one sees the same institution.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan writes, 'Sometimes the ancestral temple is named, sometimes the royal quarters, sometimes the Bright Hall—by citing them in turn one sees a single institution.

sentences.zh: 』然則三代明堂，其制一也。

translations.literal: ' Thus the Bright Halls of the Three Dynasties were one in institution.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus the Bright Halls of the Three Dynasties shared one design.

sentences.zh: 案周與夏殷，損益不同，至於明堂，因而弗革，明五室之義，得天數矣。

translations.literal: Examining Zhou against Xia and Yin, additions and subtractions differ; yet as to the Bright Hall they followed without change—making clear the meaning of five chambers accords with Heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou altered many things that Xia and Yin had done, yet left the Bright Hall unchanged; the five chambers embody Heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 是以鄭玄又曰：五室者，象五行也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zheng Xuan also says: the five chambers represent the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says the five chambers symbolize the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 然則九階者，法九土；

translations.literal: Thus the nine steps take the Nine Lands as their model;
translations.idiomatic: The nine steps then take the Nine Lands as their model;

sentences.zh: 四戶者，達四時；

translations.literal: the four doors reach the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: the four doors open to the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 八窗者，通八風。

translations.literal: the eight windows connect with the eight winds.
translations.idiomatic: the eight windows admit the eight winds.

sentences.zh: 誠不易之大範，有國之恒式。

translations.literal: Truly this is a great norm not to be altered lightly, the constant pattern of a state.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed a great and unchanging norm, the enduring form of a realm.

sentences.zh: 若其上圓下方以則天地，通水環宮以節觀者，茅蓋白盛為之質飾，赤綴白綴為之戶牖，皆典籍所具載，制度之明義也。

translations.literal: If above it is round and below square to take Heaven and Earth as its model, and a channel of water encircles the palace to regulate the sight of observers; thatched covering and white earth for its substance and ornament, red and white pendants for its doors and windows—all are fully recorded in the classics, clear principles of institution.
translations.idiomatic: That it should be round above and square below, taking Heaven and Earth as its model; that water should ring the palace to set bounds for viewers; that thatch and white earth should form its substance and red and white pendants its doors and windows—all this the classics record as the clear meaning of the institution.

sentences.zh: 在秦之世，焚滅五典，毀黜三代，變更先聖，不依舊憲。

translations.literal: In the age of Qin the Five Classics were burned, the Three Dynasties were cast down, the former sages were changed, and the old constitution was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the Five Classics were burned, the institutions of the Three Dynasties were cast aside, and the sages of old were replaced without regard to the ancient constitution.

sentences.zh: 故呂氏月令見九室之義，大戴之禮著十二堂之論。

translations.literal: Hence the Monthly Ordinances of Master Lü preserve the meaning of nine chambers, and the Rites of the Elder Dai set forth the theory of twelve halls.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Master Lü's Monthly Ordinances preserve the idea of nine chambers, and the Elder Dai's Rites advance the theory of twelve halls.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦法，亦未能改，東西二京，俱為九室。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin law and likewise could not reform it; both capitals east and west alike had nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Han took over Qin law and could not restore the ancient form; both the eastern and western capitals used nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 是以黃圖、白虎通，蔡邕、應劭等，咸稱九室以象九州，十二堂以象十二辰。

translations.literal: Thus the Yellow Chart, the Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall, Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others all say that nine chambers represent the Nine Provinces and twelve halls the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Chart, the White Tiger Hall discussions, Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others all hold that nine chambers stand for the Nine Provinces and twelve halls for the twelve chronograms.

sentences.zh: 夫室以祭天，堂以布政。

translations.literal: Chambers are for sacrificing to Heaven; halls are for issuing government.
translations.idiomatic: Chambers serve Heaven in sacrifice; halls serve the realm in governance.

sentences.zh: 依天而祭，故室不過五；

translations.literal: Sacrificing according to Heaven, therefore chambers do not exceed five;
translations.idiomatic: Because sacrifice follows Heaven, chambers should be no more than five;

sentences.zh: 依時布政，故堂不踰四。

translations.literal: issuing government according to the seasons, therefore halls do not exceed four.
translations.idiomatic: because governance follows the seasons, halls should be no more than four.

sentences.zh: 州之與辰，非所可法，九與十二，其用安在？

translations.literal: Provinces and chronograms are not models to be followed—what use have nine and twelve?
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and chronograms are not proper models—of what use are nine and twelve?

sentences.zh: 今聖朝欲尊道訓民，備禮化物，宜則五室，以為永制。

translations.literal: Now the holy court wishes to honor the Way, instruct the people, complete the rites, and transform through culture—it should take five chambers as the everlasting institution.
translations.idiomatic: If the court now means to honor the Way, teach the people, complete the rites, and transform by culture, it should adopt five chambers as the permanent form.

sentences.zh: 至如廟學之嫌，臺沼之雜，袁準之徒已論正矣，遺論具在，不復須載。」

translations.literal: As for the objections concerning temple schools and the confusion of terraces and ponds, Yuan Zhun and others have already argued them correctly; the surviving discussions are at hand and need not be cited again."
translations.idiomatic: As for objections about combining temple and school or mixing terraces with ponds, Yuan Zhun and others have already refuted them; those earlier arguments remain on record and need not be repeated here."

sentences.zh: 尋以本官行東郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing office, he administered the affairs of Administrator of Eastern Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he acted as Administrator of Eastern Commandery while retaining his court rank.

sentences.zh: 遷前軍將軍、行夏州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Forward General and administered the affairs of Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Forward General and assigned to administer Xia province.

sentences.zh: 好立條教，所在有績。

translations.literal: He liked to establish regulations and instructions; wherever he served he had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of laying down clear rules and instructions, and wherever he served he left a record of accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 轉太子僕，遷廷尉少卿，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Steward of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and given the additional rank of General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Steward of the Heir Apparent, then Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, with the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Right General and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Right General and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 初，軌深為郭祚所知，祚常謂子景尚曰：「封軌、高綽二人，並幹國之才，必應遠至。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gui was deeply appreciated by Guo Zuo; Zuo often said to his son Jing Shang: "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo, these two men, are both talents who can sustain the state—they are sure to reach far.
translations.idiomatic: From early on Gui won the deep esteem of Guo Zuo, who often told his son Jing Shang, "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo are both men of state-building talent; they are bound to rise far.

sentences.zh: 吾平生不妄進舉，而每薦此二公，非直為國進賢，亦為汝等將來之津梁也。

translations.literal: All my life I do not rashly advance recommendations, yet each time I recommend these two lords—it is not only to advance worthies for the state, but also to provide you with bridges for the future.
translations.idiomatic: In all my years I have never promoted anyone lightly, yet I have repeatedly recommended these two gentlemen—not only to advance worthy men for the realm, but also to lay down a bridge for your future.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was he valued.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 軌既以方直自業，高綽亦以風概立名。

translations.literal: Gui had already made uprightness and rectitude his profession; Gao Chuo also established his name through spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had built his career on square dealing and integrity, and Gao Chuo too had made his name through force of character.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇拜司徒，綽送迎往來，軌竟不詣。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister of State Affairs Gao Zhao was appointed Grand Minister of Education, Chuo went back and forth in sending off and welcoming him; Gui to the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao, Chief Minister of State Affairs, was appointed Grand Minister of Education, Chuo attended every ceremony of farewell and welcome—but Gui never went at all.

sentences.zh: 綽顧不見軌，乃遽歸，曰：「吾一生自謂無愆規矩，今日舉措，不如封生遠矣。

translations.literal: Chuo looked around and did not see Gui; he then hurried home and said: "All my life I have thought myself without fault against rule and measure; today's conduct falls far short of Master Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo looked about and, not seeing Gui, hurried home. "All my life I have believed myself without breach of propriety," he said, "but in today's conduct I am far behind Master Feng.

sentences.zh: 」軌以務德慎言，修身之本，姦回讒佞，世之巨害，乃為務德、慎言、遠佞、防姦四戒，文多不載。

translations.literal: " Gui took striving in virtue and caution in speech as the root of self-cultivation, and treachery, slander, and flattery as the great harms of the age; he therefore composed four admonitions—Strive in Virtue, Be Cautious in Speech, Keep Flatterers at a Distance, and Guard against Treachery—the text is largely not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Gui held that cultivating virtue and guarding one's words were the foundations of personal conduct, while treachery, slander, and flattery were the great plagues of the age. He therefore wrote four admonitions—on striving in virtue, caution in speech, keeping flatterers at a distance, and guarding against treachery—but most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 軌長子偉伯，字君良。

translations.literal: Gui's eldest son Wei Bo, styled Junliang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's eldest son Wei Bo, whose style name was Junliang.

sentences.zh: 博學有才思，弱冠除太學博士，每朝廷大議，偉伯皆預焉。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and with literary talent, at weak-crown he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University; whenever the court held great deliberations, Wei Bo took part in them.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and gifted in composition, he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University at twenty and took part in every major court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 雅為太保崔光、僕射游肇所知賞。

translations.literal: He was properly known and appreciated by Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs You Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Director You Zhao held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 太尉、清河王懌辟參軍事，懌親為孝經解詁，命偉伯為難例九條，皆發起隱漏。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi, recruited him as staff officer for military affairs; Yi personally composed a commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety and ordered Wei Bo to raise nine difficult cases—all of them exposing hidden omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, recruited him as a staff officer. When the prince personally wrote a commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, he asked Wei Bo to propose nine difficult cases, each of which exposed points the commentary had passed over in silence.

sentences.zh: 偉伯又討論禮、傳、詩、易疑事數十條，儒者咸稱之。

translations.literal: Wei Bo also discussed several dozen doubtful points in the Rites, the Commentary, the Odes, and the Changes; Confucian scholars all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo also addressed several dozen disputed questions in the Rites, the Commentary, the Odes, and the Changes, and scholars everywhere praised his work.

sentences.zh: 尋將經始明堂，廣集儒學，議其制度。

translations.literal: Soon they were about to begin constructing the Bright Hall; Confucian scholars were broadly gathered to deliberate its institution.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court planned to begin work on the Bright Hall, and scholars were summoned from far and wide to debate its design.

sentences.zh: 九五之論，久而不定。

translations.literal: The debate over nine and five long went unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The dispute over the nine-and-five arrangement dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 偉伯乃搜檢經緯，上明堂圖說六卷。

translations.literal: Wei Bo then searched through the classics and weft texts and submitted six fascicles of illustrated explanations of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo combed the classics and their apocrypha and submitted six fascicles of illustrated explanations of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 正光末，尚書僕射蕭寶夤以為關西行臺郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiao Baoyin appointed him Western Branch Office Attendant of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, Vice Director Xiao Baoyin made him an attendant in the Western Branch Office of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤為逆，偉伯乃與南平王冏潛結關中豪右韋子粲等謀舉義兵。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Wei Bo then secretly joined with Prince of Nanping Yuan Tong and the powerful men of Guanzhong such as Wei Zican to plot raising righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin turned rebel, Wei Bo secretly joined Prince of Nanping Yuan Tong and Guanzhong magnates including Wei Zican in a plan to raise loyalist forces.

sentences.zh: 事發見殺，年三十六，時人惜之。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed he was killed; he was thirty-six years old, and men of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and he was executed at the age of thirty-six; contemporaries mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 永安中，追贈散騎常侍、征虜將軍、瀛州刺史，聽一子出身。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era, posthumously he was given Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Governor of Ying province, and one son was permitted entry into office.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he was posthumously made Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Governor of Ying, and one son was granted entry into official service.

sentences.zh: 偉伯無子，轉授第三弟翼。

translations.literal: Wei Bo had no son; the privilege was transferred to his third younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo left no son, so the privilege passed to his third brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 偉伯撰封氏本錄六卷，并詩賦碑誄雜文數十篇。

translations.literal: Wei Bo composed six fascicles of the Basic Record of the Feng Clan, together with several dozen pieces of poetry, rhapsodies, stele inscriptions, dirges, and miscellaneous writings.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo wrote six fascicles of the Basic Record of the Feng Clan, along with several dozen poems, rhapsodies, stele inscriptions, dirges, and other essays.

sentences.zh: 偉伯弟業，字君脩。

translations.literal: Wei Bo's younger brother Ye, styled Junxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo's younger brother Ye, whose style name was Junxiu.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請，領殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance, concurrently Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance and concurrently as Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 業弟翼，字君贊。

translations.literal: Ye's younger brother Yi, styled Junzan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger brother Yi, whose style name was Junzan.

sentences.zh: 美容貌，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: Fine in appearance; his waist belt was ten wraps.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in appearance, with a waist so thick the belt wrapped ten times around it.

sentences.zh: 以兄偉伯立節之勳，除給事中。

translations.literal: Because of his elder brother Wei Bo's merit in upholding integrity, he was appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his elder brother Wei Bo's merit in dying for principle, he was made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 後加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was given the additional rank of General Who Raises Morale.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the additional title General Who Raises Morale.

sentences.zh: 武定初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 翼弟述，字君義。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Shu, styled Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Shu, whose style name was Junyi.

sentences.zh: 武定末，廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he served as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 述弟詢，字景文。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Xun, whose style name was Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 尚書起部郎。

translations.literal: Registrar of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Registrar of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高敬侯才鑒明遠，見機而作，身名俱劭，世載人英，天所贊也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Marquis Jing of Gao had talent and discernment bright and far-reaching; he saw the moment and acted—body and name both splendid; generation after generation bore men of excellence; Heaven approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Marquis Jing of Gao possessed keen judgment and foresight; he seized the moment and acted, winning glory in life and in name. His house produced men of excellence generation after generation—a blessing from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 崔逞文學器識，當年之俊，慮遠忽微，俱以為禍。

translations.literal: Cui Cheng had literary learning and breadth of insight, a leading man of his age; he planned far yet neglected the small—both brought disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cheng combined literary brilliance with real insight and stood among the foremost men of his day, yet his far-reaching schemes overlooked small dangers—and both failings proved fatal.

sentences.zh: 賾有茲休烈，厥世不延。

translations.literal: Ze had such splendid achievements; his generation was not prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: Ze achieved such distinction, yet his line did not endure.

sentences.zh: 封懿獲全為幸，回乃克光家，世不乏人矣。

translations.literal: Feng Yi escaped intact and was fortunate; Hui was able to glorify the family—the age never lacked men.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi was fortunate to survive with his life intact, while Hui was able to bring honor to the clan—the Feng family never lacked worthy men.

translations.idiomatic: Regarding "descendant of Grand Tutor Bao of Han": Qian's Textual Variants, juan 28, states, "The Tables of Chancellors' Lineages in the Tang History

translations.literal: 〈Juan seven, lower fascicle〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Juan 7, Part B〉

sentences.zh: 後漢渤海太守高洪，居渤海蓨縣，『四世孫裒，字宣仁，太子太傅』，此即湖之祖也。

translations.literal: Later Han Administrator of Bohai Gao Hong, dwelling in Tiao county, Bohai, "fourth-generation descendant Bao, styled Xuanren, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent"—this is Hu's ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: records that Gao Hong, Administrator of Bohai in Later Han, lived in Tiao county, Bohai: "fourth-generation descendant Bao, styled Xuanren, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent"—this is the ancestor of Gao Hu.

sentences.zh: 此『太傅』上當有『太子』二字。

translations.literal: Above this "Grand Tutor" there ought to be the two characters "Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: The two characters "Heir Apparent" must have stood before "Grand Tutor."

sentences.zh: 漢時太傅為上公，除授者甚少，安得『高裒』其人乎？

translations.literal: In Han times Grand Tutor was a supreme lord; appointees were very few—how could there be a man "Gao Bao"?
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Grand Tutor was a supreme dignity rarely conferred—how could a man named Gao Bao have held it?

sentences.zh: 」按這種祖先官爵大抵據子孫所編的譜牒，多不可信。

translations.literal: " Note: such ancestral offices and ranks are mostly based on genealogies compiled by descendants and are largely unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: " Such ancestral offices and ranks were mostly drawn from genealogies compiled by later descendants and are largely unreliable.

sentences.zh: 不僅漢無官居太傅的高裒，連「太子太傅」也難究詰。

translations.literal: Not only was there no Gao Bao who held office as Grand Tutor in Han; even "Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent" is hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Not only is there no record of a Gao Bao who served as Grand Tutor in Han, but even the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 天安中 張森楷云：「據下云『高宗深重之』，『天安』是顯祖

translations.literal: In Tian'an — Zhang Senkai states: "According to the passage below, 'Emperor Gaozong held him in deep esteem'—'Tian'an' is Emperor Xianzu's
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "in Tian'an": Zhang Senkai writes, "The passage below says 'Emperor Gaozong held him in deep esteem'—'Tian'an' is the reign era of Emperor Xianzu

translations.idiomatic: 〈Tuoba Hong〉

translations.idiomatic: reign era.

sentences.zh: 疑『天安』為『太安』之誤。

translations.literal: I suspect "Tian'an" is an error for "Tai'an."
translations.idiomatic: I suspect "Tian'an" is a corruption of "Tai'an."

sentences.zh: 『太安』是高宗

translations.literal: "Tai'an" is Emperor Gaozong's
translations.idiomatic: "Tai'an" is the reign era of Emperor Gaozong

translations.literal: 〈Tuoba Jun, Emperor Gaozong〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Tuoba Jun〉

translations.idiomatic: third reign era."

translations.literal: Posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the five provinces of Qing, Xu, Qi, Ji, and Yan
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, and supreme command over all military affairs in Qing, Xu, Qi, Ji, and Yan
