translations.idiomatic: 〈through〉

sentences.zh: 青州刺史 諸本上「青」字作「壽」。

translations.literal: Governor of Qing province — in various editions the character "qing" is written as "shou."
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Qing province: various editions read "qing" as "shou."

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷二八云：「『壽』當作『青』，地形志無壽州。

translations.literal: Qian's Textual Variants, juan 28, states: "'Shou' should be 'qing'; the Treatise on Geography has no Shou province.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's Textual Variants, juan 28, states, "'Shou' should read 'qing'; the Treatise on Geography lists no Shou province.

sentences.zh: 」按錢說是，所贈刺史是青州，都督諸州的第一州照例為所任刺史之州。

translations.literal: " Note: Qian's view is correct; the posthumously granted governorship was Qing province, and the first province among those commanded is by rule the province of the governor's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian is correct: the posthumous governorship was Qing, and the first province listed among those commanded is by convention the province in which the appointee served as governor.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 何往非善 冊府卷八九五

translations.literal: Where one goes is not ungood — Cefu, juan 895
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "where one goes is not ungood": Cefu, juan 895

sentences.zh: 〈一０五九三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page ten thousand five hundred ninety-three〉
"Go" is written as "know."
translations.idiomatic: reads "go" (wang) as "know" (zhi).

sentences.zh: 按鄰伍是勸他遷居，不是阻他遷居或出行，「往」字答非所問。

translations.literal: Note: the neighbors were urging him to move, not blocking his moving or going out—the character "go" does not answer what was asked.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbors were urging him to move, not trying to stop him from moving or traveling; "go" does not answer the question at hand.

sentences.zh: 疑作「知」是。

translations.literal: I suspect writing "know" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Know" is probably the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 子嶽武定末侍中太傅公 按北齊書卷一三清河王岳傳武定六年除太尉，至高洋稱帝後，天保五年，進太保。

translations.literal: Son Yue, at the end of Wuding, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Tutor — Note: Beiqishu, juan 13, biography of Prince of Qinghe Yue, states that in the sixth year of Wuding he was appointed Grand Commandant; after Gao Yang took the throne, in the fifth year of Tianbao he was advanced to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Yue, at the end of Wuding, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Tutor": the biography of Prince of Qinghe Yue in Beiqishu, juan 13, records that in Wuding year 6 he was made Grand Commandant, and after Gao Yang proclaimed himself emperor, in Tianbao year 5 he was promoted to Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 他從未為太傅，「傅」字當是「尉」之訛。

translations.literal: He was never Grand Tutor; the character "tutor" must be a corruption of "commandant."
translations.idiomatic: He never served as Grand Tutor; "tutor" (fu) is a corruption of "commandant" (wei).

translations.literal: 〈Deficient〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna〉

sentences.zh: 帶金城太守神龜初卒 原文上不注「闕」字，和上文「卒贈龍驤將軍、涇州刺史」句相連，不提行。

translations.literal: Concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui — the original text does not mark "lacuna" above; it connects with the preceding sentence "died; posthumously given General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Jing province" without a new line.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui: the original text does not mark a lacuna above but runs this phrase together with the preceding "died; posthumously made General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Jing" without a line break.

sentences.zh: 按前已記「卒」，下又說「神龜初卒」，哪有一人「卒」二次之理！

translations.literal: Note: earlier "died" is already recorded, and below it again says "died at the beginning of Shengui"—how can one man "die" twice!
translations.idiomatic: "Died" is already recorded above, and below we read "died at the beginning of Shengui"—surely one man cannot die twice!

sentences.zh: 且金城郡屬河州，不屬涇州

translations.literal: Moreover Jincheng commandery belongs to He province, not Jing province
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jincheng commandery belonged to He province, not Jing

sentences.zh: 〈見卷一０六下地形志下〉

translations.literal: 〈see juan one hundred six, lower, Treatise on Geography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see Treatise on Geography, Part B, juan 106〉

sentences.zh: ，不可能以涇州刺史帶金城太守。

translations.literal: , so it is impossible for a Governor of Jing province concurrently to hold Administrator of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: ; a Governor of Jing could not concurrently hold the post of Administrator of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 又北魏帶太守的例為州之長史、別駕和戍主，刺史也不會有「帶太守」是名號。

translations.literal: Moreover in Northern Wei the precedent for concurrently holding an administrator's title applies to a province's chief administrator, administrator-in-chief, and garrison commander; a governor would not have "concurrent administrator" as a title.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Wei, concurrent administrator titles were normally held by a province's chief administrator, administrator-in-chief, or garrison commander—not by a governor; "concurrent administrator" is not a governor's title.

sentences.zh: 因知此處所述實是二人。

translations.literal: Hence one knows that what is described here is in fact two men.
translations.idiomatic: This passage therefore describes two different men.

sentences.zh: 所云「卒，贈龍驤將軍、涇州刺史」者是高真，其「帶金城太守，神龜初卒」者乃另一人，傳脫去其名和歷官事迹，和上文相連，以致語不可解。

translations.literal: What says "died; posthumously given General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Jing province" refers to Gao Zhen; what says "concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui" is another man—the biography has lost his name and record of offices and connected it with the text above, making the language unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: "Died; posthumously made General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Jing" refers to Gao Zhen; "concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui" refers to another man whose name and career have dropped out of the biography and been run together with the preceding text, leaving the passage unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 今提行上注「闕」字。

translations.literal: Now a new line is begun and "lacuna" is marked above.
translations.idiomatic: A line break is introduced here and the lacuna is marked above.

sentences.zh: 參下校記[八]。

translations.literal: Compare collation note [8] below.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note [8] below.

sentences.zh: 永興末 按「永興」乃拓跋嗣年號

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxing — Note: "Yongxing" is Tuoba Si's reign era
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "at the end of Yongxing": "Yongxing" was the reign era of Tuoba Si

sentences.zh: 〈四０八－四一三〉

translations.literal: 〈four hundred eight through four hundred thirteen〉

sentences.zh: ，後來元脩曾改元永興

translations.literal: , later Yuan Xiu once changed the era name to Yongxing
translations.idiomatic: ; later Yuan Xiu briefly adopted Yongxing as an era name

sentences.zh: 〈五三二〉

translations.literal: 〈five hundred thirty-two〉

sentences.zh: ，旋即發覺重了上代年號，又改「永熙」。

translations.literal: , and immediately discovered it duplicated a previous reign era, so he changed it again to "Yongxi."
translations.idiomatic: , but soon found that it duplicated an earlier reign era and changed it to "Yongxi."

sentences.zh: 元脩的「永興」，不過幾天，談不上「初」或「末」。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu's "Yongxing" lasted only a few days—one cannot speak of "beginning" or "end."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu's "Yongxing" lasted only a few days, so "beginning" or "end" cannot apply.

sentences.zh: 上文稱貫父仁死於正光中

translations.literal: Above it says Guan's father Ren died in the Zhenguang era
translations.idiomatic: The passage above states that Guan's father Ren died during Zhenguang

sentences.zh: 〈五一九－五二四〉

translations.literal: 〈five hundred nineteen through five hundred twenty-four〉

sentences.zh: ，這裏「永興」當是「永熙」之訛。

translations.literal: , so here "Yongxing" must be a corruption of "Yongxi."
translations.idiomatic: ; "Yongxing" here must be a corruption of "Yongxi."

sentences.zh: 拔弟䐗兒 諸本於䐗兒傳末有宋人校語云：「傳無拔事，而載拔弟䐗兒，不知拔何人也。」

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Zher'er — various editions at the end of Zher'er's biography have a Song-dynasty collation note stating: "The biography has no account of Ba, yet records Ba's younger brother Zher'er—one does not know who Ba was."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Ba's younger brother Zher'er": at the end of Zher'er's biography various editions carry a Song-dynasty collation note: "The biography records nothing about Ba, yet gives an account of Ba's younger brother Zher'er—who Ba was remains unknown."

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證，未說明出於宋人校語。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Dian edition places this in textual verification without noting that it comes from a Song-dynasty collation note.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Dian edition includes this in its textual verification without identifying it as a Song-dynasty collation note.〉

sentences.zh: 按上文「帶金城太守，神龜初卒」者當即是拔。

translations.literal: Note: the man above who "concurrently held Administrator of Jincheng and died at the beginning of Shengui" should be Ba.
translations.idiomatic: The man described above as "concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui" is probably Ba.

sentences.zh: 其人應是高真子，高仁父。

translations.literal: That man should be Gao Zhen's son and Gao Ren's father.
translations.idiomatic: He was likely the son of Gao Zhen and father of Gao Ren.

sentences.zh: 據下文，䐗兒孫永樂。

translations.literal: According to the text below, Zher'er's grandson is Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: According to the text below, Zher'er's grandson was Yongle.

sentences.zh: 永樂，北齊書卷一四有傳，乃高歡從祖兄子，則其祖䐗兒、伯祖拔乃高歡伯叔輩。

translations.literal: Yongle has a biography in Beiqishu, juan 14; he was Gao Huan's elder cousin's son—thus his grandfather Zher'er and great-uncle Ba were of Gao Huan's father's and uncles' generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle has a biography in Beiqishu, juan 14; he was the son of Gao Huan's elder cousin, so his grandfather Zher'er and great-uncle Ba belonged to the same generation as Gao Huan's father and uncles.

sentences.zh: 高真是高歡伯祖

translations.literal: Gao Zhen was Gao Huan's father's father's elder brother
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhen was Gao Huan's great-uncle

sentences.zh: 〈歡祖謐之兄〉

translations.literal: 〈elder brother of Huan's grandfather, posthumous name Shi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈elder brother of Huan's grandfather Shi〉

sentences.zh: ，其子正應為歡之伯叔，輩行相當。

translations.literal: , so his sons should properly be Huan's father's uncles—the generations match.
translations.idiomatic: ; his sons would properly rank as Huan's father's uncles—the generations align.

sentences.zh: 因疑上文「涇州刺史」下脫去「子拔」和歷官事迹，只殘留「帶金城太守，神龜初卒」九字。

translations.literal: Hence I suspect that below "Governor of Jing province" the words "son Ba" and the record of offices were lost, leaving only the nine characters "concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore suspect that after "Governor of Jing province" the text originally read "son Ba" and gave his career, but only the nine characters "concurrent Administrator of Jincheng, died at the beginning of Shengui" survive.

sentences.zh: 正因拔在河州任官，故拔子仁亦為河州別駕，而拔弟徽後來被河州當地士夫推為「行河州事」以抗變亂軍，情事亦合。

translations.literal: Precisely because Ba held office in He province, Ba's son Ren also became Administrator-in-Chief of He province, and Ba's younger brother Hui was later pushed by local gentlemen of He province to "administer the affairs of He province" to resist mutinous troops—the circumstances also fit.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ba served in He province, his son Ren became Administrator-in-Chief of He, and his younger brother Hui was later chosen by local gentry in He to "administer the affairs of He province" against rebel troops—all of which fits.

sentences.zh: 顯國弟達武定中驃騎將軍行滄州事 墓誌集釋有高建墓誌

translations.literal: Xiangguo's younger brother Da, in Wuding, General of Agile Cavalry administering the affairs of Cang province — Epitaph Collection and Interpretation contains Gao Jian's epitaph
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Xiangguo's younger brother Da, in Wuding General of Agile Cavalry administering Cang province": the Epitaph Collection and Interpretation includes the epitaph of Gao Jian

sentences.zh: 〈圖版三０九〉

translations.literal: 〈illustration plate three hundred nine〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 309〉

sentences.zh: ，稱曾祖湖，祖拔，父猛。

translations.literal: , naming great-grandfather Hu, grandfather Ba, and father Meng.
translations.idiomatic: ; it names his great-grandfather Hu, grandfather Ba, and father Meng.

sentences.zh: 敍高建的終官為「行滄州事」。

translations.literal: The epitaph records Gao Jian's final office as "Administering the Affairs of Cang Province."
translations.idiomatic: The epitaph gives Gao Jian's last post as "Administering the Affairs of Cang Province."

sentences.zh: 誌之拔即此傳之高湖子、高達祖各拔。

translations.literal: The Ba in the epitaph is precisely this biography's Gao Hu's son and Gao Da's grandfather, each named Ba.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba named in the epitaph is Gao Hu's son and Gao Da's grandfather in this biography—both men were named Ba.

sentences.zh: 〈非「拔弟䐗兒」之拔，一為湖子，一為湖孫，各拔乃鮮卑名，不嫌伯姪同名。〉

translations.literal: 〈This is not the Ba of "Ba's younger brother Zher'er"; one is Hu's son and one is Hu's grandson; each Ba is a Xianbei name, and uncle and nephew sharing the same name is not objectionable.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈This is not the Ba of "Ba's younger brother Zher'er"; one is Hu's son and the other Hu's grandson. Ba was a Xianbei personal name, so there is no difficulty with uncle and nephew bearing the same name.〉

sentences.zh: 誌之猛即傳之高達父猛虎。

translations.literal: The Meng in the epitaph is this biography's Gao Da's father Meng Hu (Fierce Tiger).
translations.idiomatic: The Meng in the epitaph is Gao Da's father, Meng Hu ("Fierce Tiger"), in this biography.

sentences.zh: 世次終官均合，故集釋七以為傳「達」字為「建」之訛。

translations.literal: Generational sequence and final office all agree; therefore Jishi 7 considers the biography's character "Da" to be a corruption of "Jian."
translations.idiomatic: The generational sequence and final office all match, so Jishi 7 takes the biography's "Da" as a corruption of "Jian."

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋又有高建妻王氏誌

translations.literal: Note: the Epitaph Collection and Interpretation also contains the epitaph of Gao Jian's wife Lady Wang
translations.idiomatic: The Epitaph Collection and Interpretation also includes the epitaph of Gao Jian's wife, Lady Wang

sentences.zh: 〈圖版三一０之二〉

translations.literal: 〈illustration plate three one zero, part two〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 310, no. 2〉

sentences.zh: 稱建為「神武皇帝再從弟」，與傳所敍高達的行輩也相符，集釋說是。

translations.literal: It calls Jian "second cousin once removed of Emperor Shenwu," which also matches the generation rank narrated for Gao Da in the biography; Jishi is correct.
translations.idiomatic: It identifies Jian as "second cousin once removed of Emperor Shenwu," which matches the generational standing ascribed to Gao Da in the biography—Jishi's reading is correct.

sentences.zh: 沃野鎮長 按「長」下疑脫「史」字，或「長」是「將」之訛。

translations.literal: Chief of Woye Garrison — Note: below "Chief" one suspects the character "shi" (administrator) is missing, or "Chief" is a corruption of "General."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Chief of Woye Garrison": the character "shi" (administrator) may have dropped out after "Chief," or "Chief" may be a corruption of "General."

sentences.zh: 嚴弟賾 南本以下諸本及北史卷二四崔逞傳「賾」都作「頤」，獨百衲本作「賾」。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Ze — in the Southern edition and subsequent editions, and in Bei Shi juan 24, Cui Cheng biography, "Ze" all appear as "Yi"; only the Baona edition has "Ze."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Yan's younger brother Ze": the Southern edition and later editions, as well as the biography of Cui Cheng in Bei Shi, juan 24, all read "Yi" instead of "Ze"; only the Baona edition preserves "Ze."

sentences.zh: 又卷二四崔玄伯附崔模傳、卷三五崔浩傳、卷一０一氐傳

translations.literal: Further: juan 24, appended biography of Cui Mo under Cui Xuanbo; juan 35, Cui Hao biography; juan 101, Di biography
translations.idiomatic: The same reading appears in the appended biography of Cui Mo under Cui Xuanbo and the biographies of Cui Hao and the Di people in juan 24, juan 35, and juan 101

translations.literal: 〈supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈text supplied〉

sentences.zh: 並作「頤」，唯卷四上世祖紀上延和二年九月戊午條作「賾」。

translations.literal: All have "Yi"; only the entry for the wuwu day, ninth month, second year of Yanhe, in Annals of the First Emperor, Part A, juan 4, reads "Ze."
translations.idiomatic: All give "Yi" except the entry for the wuwu day of the ninth month of Yanhe 2 in the Annals of Emperor Shizu, Part A (juan 4), which reads "Ze."

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋盧令媛墓誌

translations.literal: Note: Epitaph Collection and Interpretation, epitaph of Lu Lingyuan
translations.idiomatic: According to the epitaph of Lu Lingyuan in the Epitaph Collection and Interpretation

sentences.zh: 〈圖版三七〉

translations.literal: 〈illustration plate three seven〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 37〉

sentences.zh: 稱曾祖度世，「夫人清河崔氏，父賾，散騎常侍、大鴻臚卿、使持節、平東將軍、青冀二州刺史、清河侯」。

translations.literal: It names great-grandfather Dushi: "Lady Cui of Qinghe; her father Ze—Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff with Extraordinary Powers, General Who Pacifies the East, Regional Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, Marquis of Qinghe."
translations.idiomatic: It names her great-grandfather Dushi and records: "Lady Cui of Qinghe; her father Ze served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff with Extraordinary Powers, General Who Pacifies the East, Regional Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Marquis of Qinghe."

sentences.zh: 歷官、封爵與此傳相符。

translations.literal: His sequence of offices and enfeoffment accord with this biography.
translations.idiomatic: The offices and titles recorded there match this biography.

sentences.zh: 知百衲本作「賾」獨是，今從之。

translations.literal: Knowing that the Baona edition alone is correct in reading "Ze," I follow it here.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Baona reading "Ze" is correct; I adopt it here.

sentences.zh: 以下他處訛「頤」均據改，不再出校記。

translations.literal: Henceforth, wherever else the erroneous "Yi" appears, I emend accordingly without issuing further collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: All other occurrences of the erroneous "Yi" are corrected on the same basis without further collation notes.

sentences.zh: 後稍遷散騎常侍 諸本「常侍」作「尚書」，北史卷二四作「常侍」。

translations.literal: Later he was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders — in various editions "Attendant" reads "Secretary"; Bei Shi juan 24 has "Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Later he was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders": most editions read "Secretary" for "Attendant," but Bei Shi, juan 24, has "Attendant."

sentences.zh: 按「散騎尚書」不知是散騎侍郎還是散騎常侍，尚書也不知何曹，魏書敍歷官一般不作如此簡稱，檢盧令媛墓誌記崔賾官位也作「散騎常侍」，別無尚書的記載

translations.literal: Note: "Secretary of the Scattered Riders" — it is unclear whether this means Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Riders or Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders; the Secretary designation is also unclear as to which bureau; the Wei Shu generally does not use such abbreviated titles when narrating offices. Checking Lu Lingyuan's epitaph, Cui Ze's office is also recorded as "Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders," with no separate record of Secretary
translations.idiomatic: "Secretary of the Scattered Riders" is ambiguous—it could mean either Attendant Gentleman or Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders, and the bureau is unclear. The Wei Shu rarely abbreviates offices in this way. Lu Lingyuan's epitaph likewise records Cui Ze as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders, with no mention of Secretary

sentences.zh: 〈見上條校記〉

translations.literal: 〈see collation note on preceding entry〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see the collation note above〉

sentences.zh: 知「尚書」乃「常侍」之訛，今據北史改。

translations.literal: Knowing "Secretary" is a corruption of "Attendant," I emend according to Bei Shi.
translations.idiomatic: "Secretary" is clearly a corruption of "Attendant"; I emend according to Bei Shi.

sentences.zh: 逞兄適 北史卷二四「適」作「遹」。

translations.literal: Cheng's elder brother Shi — Bei Shi juan 24 reads "Shi" as "Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Cheng's elder brother Shi": Bei Shi, juan 24, reads "Yu" for "Shi."

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「據其字『寧祖』，似以作『遹』為是。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai said: "Based on his style name 'Ningzu,' it seems correct to write 'Yu.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai observed: "Given his style name Ningzu, 'Yu' appears to be the correct reading."

sentences.zh: 」按「遹」有紹述、繼承之義，張說是。

translations.literal: " Note: "Yu" carries the senses of carrying forward and inheriting—Zhang is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's reasoning holds: "Yu" carries the sense of carrying on and inheriting.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文 百衲本、南本、汲本、局本「文」作「孝」，汲、局二本下注「一作『文』」。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wen — Baona, Southern, Ji, and Bureau editions read "Wen" as "Xiao"; the Ji and Bureau editions note below "also written 'Wen'."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the posthumous title Wen: the Baona, Southern, Ji, and Bureau editions read Xiao instead; the Ji and Bureau editions add a note reading "also written Wen."

sentences.zh: 北、殿二本及北史卷二四封懿傳附見封興之作「文」。

translations.literal: The Northern and Dian editions, and Bei Shi juan 24, appended biography of Feng Yi, mention of Feng Xing, read "Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern and Dian editions, as well as the mention of Feng Xing in the appended biography of Feng Yi in Bei Shi, juan 24, read Wen.

sentences.zh: 按唐書卷七一下宰相世系表也作「文」。

translations.literal: Note: Tang Shu, juan 71, Part B, Tables of Prime Ministers by Generation, also reads "Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The Tables of Prime Ministers in Tang Shu, juan 71, Part B, likewise read Wen.

sentences.zh: 這裏「孝」字當是下行「孝琬」的「孝」字錯簡而誤，今從北、殿本。

translations.literal: Here the character "Xiao" must be a misplaced slip from the "Xiao" in "Xiao Wan" in the line below; I follow the Northern and Dian editions.
translations.idiomatic: The character Xiao here was probably displaced from Xiaowan in the next line; I follow the Northern and Dian editions.

sentences.zh: 子孝琬字子倩 百衲本、南本、汲本無「孝」字，北本、殿本及北史卷二四封懿傳附孝琬有，又「子倩」作「士倩」。

translations.literal: Son Xiaowan, style name Ziqian — Baona, Southern, and Ji editions lack "Xiao"; Northern and Dian editions and Bei Shi juan 24, appended biography of Xiaowan, have it; moreover "Ziqian" reads "Shiqian."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "His son Xiaowan, style name Ziqian": the Baona, Southern, and Ji editions omit Xiao, while the Northern and Dian editions and the biography of Xiaowan in Bei Shi, juan 24, include it; some texts read Shiqian for Ziqian.

sentences.zh: 按北齊書卷二一封隆之傳作「孝琬字子倩」。

translations.literal: Note: Beiqishu, juan 21, biography of Feng Longzhi, reads "Xiaowan, style name Ziqian."
translations.idiomatic: Beiqishu, juan 21, biography of Feng Longzhi, gives "Xiaowan, style name Ziqian."

sentences.zh: 此傳百衲等本孝琬的「孝」字錯簡在上行，今從北、殿本。

translations.literal: In this biography the "Xiao" of Xiaowan in the Baona and related editions was misplaced in the preceding line; I follow the Northern and Dian editions.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baona and related editions, Xiaowan's Xiao was displaced into the line above; I follow the Northern and Dian editions.

sentences.zh: 又下文「孝琬弟孝琰」，上「孝」字，百衲等本訛作「子」，也從北、殿本。

translations.literal: Further, in the line below "Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan," the initial "Xiao" in the Baona and related editions is corruptly written as "Zi"; I likewise follow the Northern and Dian editions.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, in "Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan" below, the Baona and related editions wrongly read Zi for the first Xiao; I follow the Northern and Dian editions there as well.

sentences.zh: 孝琬之字則北齊書也作「子倩」，今從百衲等本。

translations.literal: As for Xiaowan's style name, Beiqishu also has "Ziqian"; I follow the Baona and related editions.
translations.idiomatic: For Xiaowan's style name, Beiqishu agrees on Ziqian; I follow the Baona and related editions.

sentences.zh: 天平中驃騎大將軍青州刺史 按北齊書卷二一封隆之附封延之傳，興和初

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Qing province in the Tianping era — Note: according to Beiqishu, juan 21, appended biography of Feng Yanzhi under Feng Longzhi, at the beginning of Xinghe
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Qing in the Tianping era": according to the biography of Feng Yanzhi appended to Feng Longzhi in Beiqishu, juan 21, at the beginning of Xinghe

sentences.zh: 〈五三九〉

translations.literal: 〈five hundred thirty-nine〉

sentences.zh: 才除中堅將軍，豈有天平中

translations.literal: he had only just been appointed General of the Center Army—how in the Tianping era could there already have been
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanzhi had only just been appointed General of the Center Army—how could he already have held office in the Tianping era

sentences.zh: 〈五三四－五三八〉

translations.literal: 〈five hundred thirty-four through five hundred thirty-eight〉

sentences.zh: 先已官驃騎大將軍之理？

translations.literal: the reason for already having held the office of General of Agile Cavalry beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: already served as General of Agile Cavalry?

sentences.zh: 北齊書稱興和二年，延之死後贈驃騎大將軍，此或是舉贈官，而年號有誤。

translations.literal: Beiqishu states that in the second year of Xinghe, after Yanzhi's death he was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry—this may be citing the posthumous office, while the era name is in error.
translations.idiomatic: Beiqishu records that in Xinghe 2, after Yanzhi's death, he was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry—the passage may refer to his posthumous title, but the era name is wrong.

sentences.zh: 又延之先是「行晉州事」，贈官是「冀州刺史」，此云「青州刺史」，也不合。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yanzhi had earlier "administered the affairs of Jin province," and the posthumous office was "Regional Inspector of Ji province"—here it says "Regional Inspector of Qing province," which also does not fit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yanzhi had earlier administered Jin province, and his posthumous title was Regional Inspector of Ji—yet this passage names him Regional Inspector of Qing, which also does not agree.
